verses.text: This is the vision Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
Heavens, hear! Earth, listen! The LORD has spoken. “I raised children and cared for them, and they rebelled against me.
An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its master's feeding trough. But Israel doesn't know me. My people don't stop to think.”

What a sinful nation, weighed down with wrongdoing! You're the offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly. They've abandoned the LORD, despised the Holy One of Israel, and turned away from him.
Why take another beating and go right on rebelling? Your whole head is sick, and your whole heart is weak.
From the soles of your feet to the top of your head, nothing is healthy. There are wounds, welts, and open sores, with no one to close them, bandage them, or soothe them with oil.
Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned. Strangers devour your land right in front of you, leaving it desolate as if foreigners had overthrown it.
Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, a hut in a melon field, a city under siege.
If the LORD of Armies hadn't left us a tiny remnant, we'd have ended up like Sodom. We'd have been like Gomorrah.
Hear the LORD's word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to our God's instruction, you people of Gomorrah!
“What do I want with all your sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I've had enough of burnt rams and the fat of well-fed animals. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, or male goats.
When you come to stand before me, who asked you to trample through my courts?
Stop bringing empty offerings. Your incense is detestable to me. New Moons, Sabbaths, assemblies. I can't stand gatherings full of evil.
I hate your New Moons and appointed feasts with all my soul. They've become a burden, and I'm tired of carrying them.
When you spread out your hands, I'll turn my eyes away. No matter how many prayers you say, I won't listen. Your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves and get clean. Get your evil deeds out of my sight. Stop doing wrong.
Learn to do good. Seek justice. Help those who are oppressed. Defend children without fathers. Plead the widow's case.”
“Come, let's reason together,” says the LORD. “Even if your sins are scarlet, they'll be white as snow. Even if they're red like crimson, they'll be like wool.
If you're willing and obey, you'll eat the good things the land produces.
But if you refuse and rebel, the sword will devour you. The LORD himself has spoken.”
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice. Righteousness lived there, and now murderers do.
Your silver has turned to slag, and your wine has been watered down.
Your rulers are rebels and friends of thieves. All of them love bribes and chase payouts. They don't defend children without fathers, and they won't hear a widow's case.
So the Lord, the GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says, “Ah, I'll free myself from those who oppose me and take vengeance on my enemies.
I'll turn my hand against you. I'll thoroughly burn away your slag and remove all your tin.
I'll restore your judges and advisers, just as you had them at the beginning. After that you'll be called ‘The City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.’
Zion will be redeemed through justice, and those who turn back through righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be broken together, and those who abandon the LORD will be consumed.
They'll be ashamed of the oaks you wanted, and you'll be humiliated by the gardens you chose.
You'll be like an oak with fading leaves, like a garden with no water.
The strong will be like tinder and their work like a spark. Both will burn together, and nobody will put out the fire.”
This is what Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days to come, the mountain of the LORD's house will stand above all the other mountains. It'll rise higher than the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will go there and say, “Come, let's go up to the LORD's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God. He'll teach us his ways, and we'll walk in his paths.” The law will go out from Zion, and the LORD's word from Jerusalem.

He'll judge between nations and settle cases for many peoples. They'll hammer their swords into plow blades and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation won't lift a sword against nation or train for war anymore.
House of Jacob, come. Let's walk in the LORD's light.

You've abandoned your people, the house of Jacob. They're full of influences from the east, with people who practice divination like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of foreigners.
Their land is full of silver and gold, with no end to their treasures. It's full of horses, with no end to their chariots.
Their land is full of idols too. They bow to the work of their own hands, to things their own fingers made.
People are brought low, and humanity is humbled. So don't forgive them.
Go into the rock and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty.
Proud looks will be lowered, and human arrogance will bow down. The LORD alone will be honored above all on that day.
The LORD of Armies has a day for everything proud and arrogant. Whatever lifts itself high will be brought low,
including all the tall, towering cedars of Lebanon and all the oaks of Bashan,
all the high mountains and every hill that rises up,
every towering lookout and every fortified wall,
all the ships of Tarshish and every lovely image.
Human pride will bow down, and arrogance will be brought low. The LORD alone will be honored above all on that day.
The idols will disappear altogether.
People will go into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground to hide from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty when he rises to shake the earth with great force.
On that day people will throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats, the idols they made for themselves to worship.
They'll go into caves in the rocks and cracks in the jagged cliffs to hide from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty when he rises to shake the earth with great force.
Stop putting your trust in people, who have only the breath in their nostrils. How much can they count for?
Look, the Lord, GOD of Armies, is taking away what Jerusalem and Judah depend on, their whole supply of bread and water,
the mighty warrior, the soldier, the judge, the prophet, the diviner, the elder,
the captain of fifty, the respected man, the adviser, the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.
I'll put boys in charge as their princes, and children will rule over them.
People will oppress one another, neighbor against neighbor. The young will act arrogantly toward the old, and the wicked toward the honorable.
A man will grab his brother in their father's house and say, “You've got clothes. You can be our ruler. Take charge of this ruin!”
That day he'll cry out, “I can't fix this. I've got no bread or clothes in my house. Don't make me ruler of the people!”
Jerusalem is ruined and Judah has fallen because their words and actions are against the LORD, defying his glory to his face.
The looks on their faces testify against them. They show off their sin like Sodom and make no effort to hide it. Trouble for them! They've brought disaster on themselves.
Tell the righteous it'll go well for them. They'll eat the fruit of what they've done.
Trouble for the wicked! Disaster is coming on them. What they've done with their own hands will come back on them.
Children oppress my people, and women rule over them. My people, your leaders steer you wrong and tear up the paths you're meant to follow.
The LORD stands up to bring his case. He rises to judge the peoples.
The LORD will call his people's elders and leaders to account. “You're the ones who devoured the vineyard. What you stole from the poor is in your houses.
What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor?” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The LORD also said, “The daughters of Zion are arrogant. They walk with their necks stretched out and their eyes flirting, taking dainty steps and jingling the jewelry on their feet.
So the Lord will bring sores on the crowns of their heads, and the LORD will make their scalps bald.”
On that day the Lord will strip away the beauty of their anklets, their headbands, their crescent necklaces,
their earrings, bracelets, and veils,
their headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume bottles, and charms,
their signet rings and nose rings,
their fine robes, capes, cloaks, and purses,
their hand mirrors, fine linen clothes, tiaras, and shawls.
Rot will replace sweet spices, a rope will replace a belt, and baldness will replace styled hair. Sackcloth will take the place of fine robes, and branding will take the place of beauty.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your mighty warriors will fall in battle.
Zion's gates will grieve and mourn. She'll sit desolate on the ground.
On that day seven women will grab hold of one man and say, “We'll eat our own food and wear our own clothes. Just let us take your name. Take away our disgrace.”
On that day the LORD's branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of Israel's survivors.
Those left in Zion and those who remain in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone listed among the living in Jerusalem.
That will happen when the Lord washes away the filth of Zion's daughters and clears the blood from Jerusalem by a spirit of justice and a spirit of burning.
The LORD will create a cloud of smoke by day and a bright blaze by night over all the homes of Mount Zion and over her gatherings. A canopy will cover all the glory.
There'll be a shelter to give shade from the day's heat and a refuge from storm and rain.
Let me sing for my beloved, a song about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill.
He dug the ground, cleared out the stones, and planted the finest vines. He built a tower in the middle and carved out a winepress. He expected good grapes, but it grew wild ones.
“Now, people of Jerusalem and Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard? When I expected grapes, why did it produce wild ones?
Now I'll tell you what I'll do to my vineyard. I'll pull out its hedge, and it'll be eaten up. I'll break down its wall, and it'll be trampled.
I'll make it a wasteland. No one will prune it or hoe it. Briers and thorns will grow, and I'll tell the clouds not to rain on it.”

The vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel. The people of Judah are the planting he delights in. He looked for justice and found oppression. He looked for righteousness and heard a cry of distress.
Trouble for those who add house to house and field to field until there's no room left and you live alone in the middle of the land!
I heard the LORD of Armies say, “Many houses will be deserted. Even the large and beautiful ones will stand empty.
Ten acres of vineyard will yield just one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will yield only an ephah.”
Trouble for those who get up early to chase strong drink and stay up late until wine sets them on fire!
They feast with harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine, but they pay no attention to what the LORD does or consider the work of his hands.
So my people go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Their honored men are starving, and their crowds are parched with thirst.
So Sheol has opened its mouth wide, its appetite without limit. Their glory, their crowds, their pomp, and those celebrating among them go down into it.
People are brought low, humanity is humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant are lowered.
But the LORD of Armies is exalted through justice, and God the Holy One shows himself holy through righteousness.
Lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat where the rich once lived.
Trouble for those who drag wrongdoing along with cords of lies and pull wickedness like a cart on a rope.
They say, “Tell him to hurry up and do his work so we can see it. Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come close so we can know what it is!”
Trouble for those who call evil good and good evil, who pass off darkness as light and light as darkness, and who swap bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!
Trouble for those who think they're wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
Trouble for those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drinks,
who take bribes to clear the guilty and deny justice to the innocent!

Just as flames consume stubble and dry grass collapses in the fire, their roots will rot and their blossoms will blow away like dust. They rejected the law of the LORD of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

The LORD's anger burns against his people. He's stretched out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains shake, and their bodies lie like garbage in the streets. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
He'll raise a banner to nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they'll come swift and fast.
None of them will tire or stumble. None will doze or sleep. No belt will come loose, and no sandal strap will break.
Their arrows are sharp and all their bows drawn. Their horses' hooves are like flint, and their wheels are like a whirlwind.
They'll roar like a lioness and like young lions. They'll roar, seize their prey, and carry it off, with no one to rescue it.
On that day they'll roar against the people like the sea. Look toward the land and there's darkness and distress. The clouds shut out the light.
In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up. The train of his robe filled the temple.
Seraphim stood above him. Each had six wings. With two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
One called to another, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
The foundations beneath the doorways shook at the sound of the one who called, and the temple filled with smoke.
I said, “I'm doomed! I'm a man with unclean lips, and I live among people with unclean lips. My eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!”
Then one of the seraphim flew to me with a burning coal in his hand. He'd taken it off the altar with tongs.
He touched my mouth with it and said, “Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is taken away, and your sin is forgiven.”
I heard the Lord ask, “Whom should I send? Who will go for us?” I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
He said, “Go and tell these people, ‘You hear, but you don't understand. You see, but you don't grasp what you're seeing.’
Make these people's hearts dull, weigh down their ears, and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back, and be healed.”
I asked, “Lord, how long?” He answered, “Until cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, houses stand empty, and the land is laid completely waste,
until the LORD has taken the people far away and many places across the land are deserted.
Even if a tenth remains, it too will be consumed. Just as a terebinth or an oak leaves a stump when it's cut down, the holy seed is the stump.”
When Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel went up to fight against Jerusalem, but they couldn't defeat it.
The house of David heard, “Syria has allied with Ephraim.” The king and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaking in the wind.
Then the LORD told Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz. Take your son Shearjashub with you to the end of the channel from the upper pool, on the road to the laundry field.
Tell him, ‘Watch yourself and stay calm. Don't be afraid or lose heart over these two smoking ends of torches, over the fierce anger of Rezin, Syria, and Remaliah's son.
Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have plotted against you. They've said,
“Let's attack Judah, tear it apart, divide it among ourselves, and put Tabeel's son on the throne.”
This is what the Lord GOD says. “Their plan won't stand. It won't happen.”
The head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered and cease to be a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son. If you won't believe, you won't stand firm.’”
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again.
“Ask the LORD your God for a sign, whether from the depths below or the heights above.”
But Ahaz said, “I won't ask. I won't put the LORD to the test.”
Isaiah said, “Listen, house of David. Isn't it enough to try people's patience? Are you going to try my God's patience too?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she'll name him Immanuel.
He'll eat butter and honey by the time he knows to reject evil and choose good.
Before the child knows to reject evil and choose good, the land of those two kings you dread will be abandoned.
The LORD will bring days on you, your people, and your father's house unlike any since Ephraim separated from Judah. He'll bring the king of Assyria.
On that day the LORD will whistle for the fly from the farthest stretches of Egypt's rivers and for the bee from the land of Assyria.
They'll come and settle in the desolate valleys, in the cracks in the rocks, on every thorn hedge, and on all the pastures.
On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the River, the king of Assyria, to shave the head and the hair of the feet. It will take off the beard too.
On that day a man will keep a young cow and two sheep alive.
They'll give so much milk that he'll eat butter. Everyone left in the land will eat butter and honey.
On that day every place that once had a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels will be covered in briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows, because the whole land will be briers and thorns.
You won't go onto any of the hills once worked with a hoe, for fear of briers and thorns. They'll become places to turn oxen loose and let sheep roam.”
The LORD told me, “Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’
I'll have trustworthy witnesses testify for me. They'll be Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.”
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. Then the LORD told me, “Name him Maher Shalal Hash Baz.
Before the boy knows how to say ‘My father’ and ‘My mother,’ the king of Assyria will carry off the riches of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria.”
The LORD spoke to me again.
“These people have rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son.
So look, the Lord is bringing against them the mighty floodwaters of the River, the king of Assyria in all his glory. The flood will rise above its channels and spill over all its banks.
It'll sweep into Judah, overflow, and pass through, rising right up to the neck. Its outspread wings will cover the whole width of your land, Immanuel.
Raise an uproar, you peoples, and be shattered! Listen, all you distant lands. Get ready for battle and be shattered! Get ready for battle and be shattered!
Make your plans together, and they'll come to nothing. Give the word, and it won't stand, because God is with us.”
The LORD spoke to me with a strong hand and warned me to stay clear of the way these people live. He said,
“Don't call everything a conspiracy just because these people do. Don't fear their threats or let them terrify you.
Honor the LORD of Armies as holy. He's the one you must fear, the one you must dread.
He'll be a sanctuary. But to both houses of Israel he'll be a stone that trips them and a rock that makes them fall. To the people of Jerusalem he'll be a trap and a snare.
Many will stumble over it, fall, and be broken. They'll be caught in the trap and taken.”
Wrap up the covenant. Seal the law among my disciples.
I'll wait for the LORD, who hides his face from the house of Jacob. I'll look for him.
Look, the children the LORD has given me and I are signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When people tell you, “Ask the mediums and sorcerers who chirp and mutter,” shouldn't a people ask their God? Should they ask the dead on behalf of the living?
Turn to the law and the covenant! If people don't speak according to this word, there's no dawn for them.
They'll pass through the land in distress and hunger. When they're hungry, they'll grow anxious and curse their king and their God. They'll turn their faces upward,
then look down at the earth and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They'll be driven into thick darkness.

But there'll be no more gloom for the land that was in anguish. In the past God brought shame on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali. In the time to come he'll make glorious the way by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light. Light has shone on those living in the land of death's shadow.
You've made the nation grow and increased their joy. They rejoice before you like people celebrating the harvest, like people dividing the spoils.
You've broken their heavy yoke, the staff on their shoulder, and the rod of the one who oppressed them, just as in the day of Midian.
All the armor worn in the noisy battle and all the clothes rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.
A child is born to us. A son is given to us. The government will rest on his shoulders. He'll be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His rule and its peace will grow without end. He'll reign on David's throne and establish and uphold his kingdom with justice and righteousness from then on, forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it fell on Israel.
All the people will know it, including Ephraim and those living in Samaria, who say with pride and arrogance in their hearts,
“The bricks have fallen, but we'll rebuild with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we'll plant cedars in their place.”
So the LORD will raise up Rezin's adversaries against Israel and stir up its enemies,
the Syrians in front and the Philistines behind. They'll devour Israel with mouths wide open. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Yet the people haven't turned back to the one who struck them. They haven't sought the LORD of Armies.
So in a single day the LORD will cut off from Israel both head and tail, palm branch and reed.
The elder and the honored man are the head. The prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
The leaders of these people lead them astray, and those who follow them are destroyed.

So the Lord won't rejoice over their young men or show compassion to their fatherless children and widows. Everyone is profane and does wrong, and every mouth talks foolishness. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Wickedness burns like fire. It consumes briers and thorns and sets the forest thickets ablaze, sending up a column of smoke.
The wrath of the LORD of Armies burns up the land, and the people are fuel for the fire. Nobody spares their own brother.
They'll devour what's on the right and still be hungry. They'll eat what's on the left and still not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of their own arm,
Manasseh devouring Ephraim, Ephraim devouring Manasseh, and both turning against Judah. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Trouble for those who make unjust laws and write decrees that oppress people,
denying justice to the needy and robbing the poor among my people of their rights, so they can plunder widows and prey on children without fathers!
What will you do on the day you're called to account, when ruin comes from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
You'll only crouch among the prisoners or fall among the slain. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Ah, Assyria, the rod of my anger! The staff in his hand is my indignation.
I'll send him against a profane nation. I'll order him to take spoils and seize plunder from the people who anger me and trample them like mud in the streets.
But that's not what he intends or what he has in mind. He wants to destroy and wipe out many nations.
He says, “Aren't all my princes kings?
Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?”
My hand seized kingdoms whose carved idols surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
Won't I do to Jerusalem and her idols what I did to Samaria and hers?
When the Lord finishes all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I'll punish the king of Assyria for what his stubborn pride has produced and for his arrogant looks.
He has said, “I did it by my own strength and wisdom, because I have understanding. I moved the boundaries of peoples and robbed their treasuries. Like a mighty warrior I brought down their rulers.
My hand found the wealth of peoples like a nest. I gathered the whole earth like someone picking up abandoned eggs. No one fluttered a wing, opened a mouth, or chirped.”

Does an ax boast over the one who chops with it? Does a saw raise itself above the one who uses it? That would be like a rod lifting those who lift it, or a staff picking up someone who isn't made of wood.
So the Lord, the GOD of Armies, will send wasting among his well-fed ones, and under his glory a fire will be kindled.
Israel's Light will become a fire and his Holy One a flame. In one day it will burn up his thorns and briers.
He'll consume the glory of his forest and his fruitful field, body and soul. It'll be like a standard-bearer collapsing.
So few trees will be left in his forest that a child could write down their number.
On that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped from Jacob's house will no longer lean on the one who struck them. They'll truly lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
Israel, even if your people are as numerous as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
The Lord, the GOD of Armies, will carry out the destruction he's decreed throughout all the earth.
So the Lord, the GOD of Armies, says, “My people who live in Zion, don't fear the Assyrian, even when he strikes you with a rod and raises his staff against you as Egypt did.
In just a little while my indignation against you will come to an end, and my anger will turn to his destruction.”
The LORD of Armies will raise a whip against him, as when Midian was struck down at the rock of Oreb. His rod will be over the sea, and he'll raise it as he did against Egypt.
On that day his burden will come off your shoulder and his yoke off your neck. The yoke will be broken because of the anointing oil.
He has reached Aiath and passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.
They've crossed the pass and taken lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry out, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is on the run. The people of Gebim flee for safety.
Today he'll halt at Nob and shake his fist at the mountain of daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, the GOD of Armies, will lop off the branches with terrifying force. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty brought low.
He'll cut down the forest thickets with iron, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
A shoot will grow from Jesse's stump, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
The LORD's Spirit will rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and might, of knowledge and fear of the LORD.
He'll delight in fearing the LORD. He won't judge by what his eyes see or decide by what his ears hear.
He'll judge the poor with righteousness and rule fairly for the humble of the earth. He'll strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he'll kill the wicked.
Righteousness and faithfulness will be like belts fastened around his waist.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze, and their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
A nursing child will play near a cobra's hole, and a weaned child will put a hand at a viper's den.
They won't hurt or destroy anywhere on my holy mountain. The earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
On that day the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner for the peoples. His resting place will be glorious.
On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He'll raise a banner for the nations, gather Israel's outcasts, and bring together the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's envy will disappear, and those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won't envy Judah, and Judah won't persecute Ephraim.
They'll swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west and together plunder the peoples of the east. They'll extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the people of Ammon will obey them.
The LORD will completely destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea. He'll wave his hand over the River with a scorching wind, split it into seven streams, and let people cross in their sandals.
There'll be a highway out of Assyria for the remnant of his people, just as there was for Israel when they came up out of Egypt.
On that day you'll say, “I thank you, LORD. Though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you comfort me.
Look, God is my salvation. I'll trust him and won't be afraid. The LORD, the LORD, is my strength and my song. He has become my salvation.”
With joy you'll draw water from the wells of salvation.
On that day you'll say, “Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the peoples what he's done! Proclaim that his name is lifted high!
Sing to the LORD, because he's done excellent things! Let the whole earth know it!
Cry out and shout, people of Zion, because the Holy One of Israel is great among you!”
This is the warning about Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a banner on the bare mountain! Shout to them! Wave them toward the gates of the nobles.
I’ve given orders to the ones I set apart. I’ve called my mighty warriors to carry out my anger, the ones who celebrate with pride.
Hear that roar in the mountains? It sounds like a huge crowd! The kingdoms of the nations are gathering, and the LORD of Armies is getting his army ready for battle.
They’re coming from a far-off land, from the farthest edge of the sky. The LORD is coming with the weapons of his anger to destroy the whole land.
Cry out! The LORD’s day is nearly here. Destruction is coming from the Almighty.
Every hand will go limp. Every heart will melt.
They’ll be terrified. Pain and grief will grab hold of them like the pains of a woman in labor. They’ll stare at each other in shock, their faces blazing.
Look, the day of the LORD is coming, harsh and fierce with anger. It’ll leave the land empty and wipe out its sinners.
The stars and constellations won’t give their light. The sun will go dark as it comes up, and the moon won’t shine.
I’ll punish the world for its evil and the wicked for the wrong they’ve done. I’ll put an end to the swagger of the proud and bring the arrogance of the ruthless way down.
I’ll make people harder to find than fine gold, harder to find than the pure gold of Ophir.
So I’ll make the skies tremble, and the earth will shake out of place when the LORD of Armies lets loose his fierce anger.
Like a hunted gazelle or sheep with nobody to gather them, everyone will turn back to their own people and run to their own land.
Anyone they find will be run through. Anyone they capture will fall by the sword.
Their babies will be dashed to pieces in front of them. Their homes will be ransacked, and their wives will be raped.
Look, I’m stirring up the Medes against them. Silver means nothing to them, and gold doesn’t interest them either.
Their bows will cut down young men. They’ll have no mercy on babies from the womb. They won’t spare children.
Babylon, the showpiece of kingdoms and the pride and joy of the Chaldeans, will end up like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
Nobody will ever live there again, generation after generation. No Arabian will pitch a tent there, and no shepherd will bed down a flock there.
Desert animals will settle in, and jackals will fill the houses. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will play there.
Hyenas will howl in the fortresses and jackals in the fancy palaces. Babylon’s time is almost up. Her days won’t be stretched out.
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob. He’ll choose Israel again and settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and become part of Jacob’s household.

Other peoples will bring them back to their place. In the LORD’s land, Israel’s household will take those people as servants, men and women. They’ll take their former captors captive and rule over the people who oppressed them.
The LORD will give you a break from your pain, your troubles, and the hard labor you were forced to do.
When that day comes, you’ll throw this taunt at Babylon’s king: “Look at that. The tyrant’s finished! The golden city is done!”
The LORD has snapped the stick of the wicked and broken the rulers’ scepter.
They struck people over and over in their rage. They ruled the nations in anger, and nobody stopped their persecution.
Now the whole earth can finally rest. It’s quiet, and people burst into song.
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon are glad you’ve fallen. “Ever since you went down, nobody’s come up here to cut us down!”
Sheol below is stirring to meet you when you get there. It wakes the spirits of the dead, all who ruled the earth. It gets every king of the nations up from his throne.
They’ll all ask you, “So you got as weak as the rest of us? You ended up just like us?”
All your glory came down to Sheol with the sound of your stringed instruments. Now maggots are your bed and worms are your blanket.
How far you’ve fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! You brought nations down, and now you’ve been cut down to the ground.
You told yourself, “I’ll climb into heaven! I’ll set my throne above God’s stars! I’ll sit on the mountain where the assembly meets, way up north!
I’ll climb higher than the clouds! I’ll make myself like the Most High!”
Down you go to Sheol, all the way to the bottom of the pit.
People will stare at you and try to take it in. “Is this the guy who made the earth shake and rattled kingdoms?
The one who turned the world into a wasteland, toppled its cities, and wouldn’t let his prisoners go home?”
All the kings of the nations lie in honor, each in his own resting place.
But you’ve been thrown out of your tomb like a rotten branch. The bodies of those run through with swords cover you as they go down to the stones of the pit. You’re like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You won’t be buried with those kings. You wrecked your land and killed your own people. The children of evildoers will never be remembered by name.
Get ready to slaughter his children for what their fathers did wrong, so they can’t rise up, take over the earth, and cover the world with cities.
“I’ll rise up against them,” says the LORD of Armies. “I’ll erase Babylon’s name, wipe out anyone who’s left, and cut off its children and grandchildren,” says the LORD.
“I’ll turn it into a home for porcupines and a place full of pools. I’ll sweep it away with the broom of destruction,” says the LORD of Armies.
The LORD of Armies has sworn, “What I’ve planned will happen. What I’ve decided will stand.
I’ll break the Assyrian in my land and trample him on my mountains. Then his yoke will come off my people, and the load he put on them will come off their shoulders.
This is the plan for the whole earth. This is the hand stretched out over every nation.
The LORD of Armies has made his plan. Who can stop it? His hand is stretched out. Who can turn it back?”
This warning came the year King Ahaz died.
All of you in Philistia, hold the celebration. That stick that struck you may be broken, but a viper will come from the snake’s root, and its offspring will be a fiery flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poorest will have food, and the needy will lie down in safety. But I’ll kill your root with famine, and whoever’s left will be killed.
Wail, gate! Cry out, city! All of Philistia is melting away. Smoke is coming out of the north, and there’s nobody falling behind in those ranks.
What answer will the nation’s messengers get? The LORD founded Zion, and the suffering among his people will find shelter there.
Here’s the warning for Moab. In a single night, Ar in Moab is wrecked and wiped out. In a single night, Kir in Moab is wrecked and wiped out.
They go up to Bayith and Dibon, up to the high places to cry. Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba. Every head is shaved. Every beard is cut off.
People wear sackcloth in the streets. In the streets and on the rooftops, everybody’s wailing and crying their eyes out.
Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. You can hear them all the way to Jahaz. Even Moab’s armed men cry out. Deep down, they’re shaking.
My heart cries out for Moab! Its nobles run to Zoar and Eglath Shelishiyah. They’re crying as they climb the road to Luhith, and on the way to Horonaim they cry out over the destruction.
The waters of Nimrim will dry up. The grass has withered, the new grass has died, and there’s nothing green left.
So they’ll haul what they’ve earned and what they’ve saved across the Brook of the Willows.
The cry has gone all around Moab’s borders. You can hear the wailing as far as Eglaim and Beer Elim.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood. And I’m bringing more trouble on Dimon: a lion for the Moabites who escape and the ones still left in the land.
Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Selah through the wilderness to Daughter Zion’s mountain.
At the Arnon crossings, the daughters of Moab will be like birds wandering around after their nest has been scattered.
Give us advice! See that justice is done! Make your shade as dark as night in the middle of the day. Hide the people who’ve been driven out. Don’t hand over anyone who’s on the run.
Let my outcasts stay with you! Give Moab somewhere to hide from the destroyer. The one who squeezes people dry will be finished, the wrecking will stop, and the oppressors will be gone from the land.
A throne will be set up in faithful love. Someone will sit on it in faithfulness in David’s tent. He’ll judge fairly, seek justice, and waste no time doing what’s right.
We’ve heard how proud Moab is. The arrogance, the swagger, the rage, all of it. Those big boasts amount to nothing.
So Moab will cry for Moab. Everyone will wail. Completely crushed, you’ll mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth.

Heshbon’s fields are dying, and so is Sibmah’s vine. The rulers of the nations broke its best branches. They used to reach as far as Jazer and stretch into the wilderness. Its shoots spread far and went across the sea.
So I’ll cry with Jazer over Sibmah’s vine. I’ll soak you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh. The battle shout has come down on your summer fruit and your harvest.
All the joy and laughter have gone out of the fruitful fields. No singing or cheering in the vineyards. Nobody’s stomping grapes in the winepresses. I’ve put a stop to the shouting.
My heart hums like a harp for Moab. Deep inside, I ache for Kir Heres.
Moab can show up and wear himself out at the high place. He can go to his sanctuary and pray. It won’t get him anywhere.
That’s what the LORD said about Moab back then.
But now the LORD says, “Within three years, counted as carefully as a worker on a contract would count them, Moab’s glory will be disgraced along with its huge crowd. The few left will be weak.”
Here’s the warning for Damascus. “Look, Damascus won’t even be a city anymore. It’ll be a pile of rubble.
The towns of Aroer are abandoned. Flocks will settle there and lie down with nobody to scare them.
Ephraim will lose its fortress, Damascus its kingdom, and the survivors of Syria will be like the glory of the people of Israel,” says the LORD of Armies.
“On that day Jacob’s glory will waste away. His well-fed body will get skinny.
It’ll be like a harvester sweeping up stalks and cutting the grain, like somebody picking up loose grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

A little will still be left, like after somebody shakes an olive tree. Two or three olives way up on the top branch, four or five on the outside branches of a fruitful tree,” says the LORD, the God of Israel.
On that day people will look to their Maker. Their eyes will turn with respect to the Holy One of Israel.
They won’t look to the altars they made by hand or give their attention to what their own fingers shaped, the Asherah poles or the incense altars.
On that day their strong cities will be like those places in the woods and up on the mountain that were abandoned as the people of Israel came through. They’ll be left desolate.
You forgot the God who saves you. You didn’t remember the rock that made you strong. So you put in beautiful plants and set out seedlings from somewhere else.
You fence them in the day you plant them. You get the seeds to bloom in the morning. But on the day of grief and unbearable sorrow, your harvest will be gone.
Listen to all those peoples roaring like the sea! Hear the nations rushing like powerful floodwaters!
The nations will come rushing like a flood, but he’ll call them out and they’ll run far away, driven like chaff on the mountains in the wind and like dust spinning ahead of a storm.
Come evening, there’s terror. Before morning, they’re gone. That’s the share of those who loot us and what’s coming to the ones who rob us.
Ah, that land where wings rustle, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia!

It sends envoys across the sea in papyrus boats, saying, “Go fast, messengers! Go to a nation of tall, smooth-skinned people, a people feared from the start, a nation that measures out and tramples down, a land split by rivers!”
Everybody in the world, everyone living on earth, look when a banner goes up on the mountains! Listen when the trumpet blows!
The LORD told me, “I’ll stay still and watch from where I live, like the clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”

Before harvest, when the flowers are gone and the blossoms have turned into grapes that are starting to ripen, he’ll take pruning hooks to the shoots. He’ll cut down the spreading branches and carry them off.
He’ll leave them all for the hungry birds of the mountains and the wild animals. The birds will feed on them all summer and the animals all winter.

Then those tall, smooth-skinned people, feared from the start, a nation that measures out and tramples down in a land split by rivers, will bring a gift to the LORD of Armies. They’ll bring it to Mount Zion, the place of his name.
Here’s the warning for Egypt. “Look, the LORD is riding a fast cloud straight to Egypt. Egypt’s idols will shake in front of him, and Egypt’s heart will melt.
I’ll turn Egyptians against Egyptians. They’ll fight brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
Egyptians will lose heart, and I’ll wreck their plans. They’ll turn to their idols, spellcasters, people who talk to spirits, and sorcerers.
I’ll hand the Egyptians over to a cruel master. A brutal king will rule them,” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The sea will run out of water, and the river will dry right up.
The rivers will stink. Egypt’s streams will shrink and dry up. The reeds and rushes will wither.
The meadows by the Nile, the plants on its banks, and every field sown along it will dry up, blow away, and be gone.
The fishers will cry. Everybody who fishes in the Nile will mourn, and the people who spread nets on the water will waste away.
The people who prepare flax and the ones who weave white cloth will be crushed.
The pillars will shatter. Everyone working for wages will grieve deep down.
The officials of Zoan are straight-up fools. Pharaoh’s smartest advisers are giving him terrible advice. How can you tell Pharaoh, “I come from wise people, from kings of long ago”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you what the LORD of Armies has planned for Egypt, if they can figure it out.
Zoan’s officials have become fools. Memphis’s officials have been fooled. The very people meant to hold Egypt’s tribes together have led Egypt off course.
The LORD has mixed a spirit of confusion into Egypt, and its leaders have steered it wrong in everything it does. Egypt staggers like a drunk person in his own vomit.
Nobody in Egypt will have any work to do, head or tail, palm branch or rush.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women trembling in fear when the LORD of Armies shakes his hand over them.
The land of Judah will terrify Egypt. Just hearing its name will scare people because of what the LORD of Armies has planned against Egypt.
On that day five cities in Egypt will speak Canaan’s language and swear allegiance to the LORD of Armies. One will be called “The City of Destruction.”
On that day there’ll be an altar to the LORD in the middle of Egypt and a pillar to the LORD at its border.
It’ll stand as a sign and a witness to the LORD of Armies in Egypt. When the Egyptians cry out to the LORD because people are oppressing them, he’ll send a savior and defender to rescue them.
The LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know him that day. They’ll worship with sacrifices and offerings. They’ll make promises to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, then heal it. They’ll come back to him, he’ll hear their pleas, and he’ll heal them.
On that day there’ll be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. Assyrians will go into Egypt, Egyptians will go into Assyria, and both will worship together.
On that day Israel will join Egypt and Assyria as the third, a blessing in the heart of the earth.
The LORD of Armies will bless them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”
In the year King Sargon of Assyria sent Tartan to Ashdod, Tartan attacked the city and took it.
Around then the LORD told Isaiah son of Amoz, “Take the sackcloth off your waist and the sandals off your feet.” Isaiah did it and went around naked and barefoot.
The LORD said, “My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a warning about Egypt and Ethiopia.
In the same way, the king of Assyria will march away captives from Egypt and exiles from Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot with their backsides exposed, to Egypt’s shame.
People will be shocked and ashamed. They put their hopes in Ethiopia and took pride in Egypt.
That day the people of this coast will say, ‘Look what happened to the ones we were counting on! We ran to them for help against Assyria’s king. How are we supposed to escape now?’”
Here’s the warning for the wilderness by the sea. Like whirlwinds sweeping through the South, it comes out of the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
A brutal vision came to me. Traitors are doing what traitors do, and the destroyer keeps destroying. Go up, Elam! Attack! I’ve put an end to all of Media’s sighing.
Anguish shoots through my thighs. Pain hits me like labor pains. It hurts so much I can’t hear, and I’m so shaken I can’t see.
My heart is racing. Horror has me scared stiff. I was looking forward to twilight, and now it’s got me shaking.
They set the table and post a guard. They eat. They drink. Get up, princes! Oil your shields!
The Lord told me, “Go post a lookout, and have him report what he sees.
When he sees a troop, riders coming in pairs, a troop on donkeys, a troop on camels, he needs to listen hard and pay close attention.”
Then he cried out like a lion, “Lord, I stand on the watchtower all day long. Every night I stay at my post.
Look, here comes a troop, riders in pairs!” Then he called out, “Babylon has fallen! Fallen! Every carved image of her gods has been smashed to the ground.
You’ve been threshed like grain on my threshing floor!” I’ve told you what I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel.
Here’s the warning for Dumah. Someone calls out to me from Seir, “Watchman, how much of the night is left? Watchman, how much of the night is left?”
The watchman says, “Morning’s coming, and so is night. If you’ve got questions, ask. Come back again.”
Here’s the warning for Arabia. You caravans of Dedanites will spend the night in the thickets of Arabia.
The people who live in Tema brought water to the thirsty and met the people on the run with bread.
They were running from swords, from the drawn blade, from the bent bow, from the heat of battle.
The Lord told me, “Within one year, counted as carefully as a worker under contract would count it, all of Kedar’s glory will be gone.
Only a few of Kedar’s mighty archers will be left.” The LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
Here’s the warning for the Valley of Vision. What’s going on with you? Why has everybody gone up to the rooftops?
You’re a city full of shouting, a noisy town, a place that loves to celebrate. But your dead didn’t die by the sword. They didn’t fall in battle.
Your rulers all ran off together. The archers tied them up. All your people who were found were tied up together, even though they’d run far away.
So I said, “Look away. I’m going to cry my heart out. Don’t wear yourself out trying to comfort me when the daughter of my people has been destroyed.
This is a day of chaos, crushing defeat, and confusion from the Lord, GOD of Armies, in the Valley of Vision. Walls are breaking down, and cries are going up to the mountains.”
Elam came with its quivers, chariots full of men, and horsemen. Kir took the cover off its shield.
Your best valleys filled up with chariots, and the riders lined up at the gate.
He stripped away Judah’s protection. That day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You saw just how many gaps there were in the walls of David’s city, and you gathered the water from the lower pool.
You counted Jerusalem’s houses and tore them down to reinforce the wall.
You made a reservoir between the two walls for water from the old pool. But you didn’t look to the one who did this or pay attention to the one who planned it long ago.
That day the Lord, GOD of Armies, called you to cry, mourn, shave your heads, and put on sackcloth.
And look at you, laughing and celebrating, slaughtering cattle and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine. “Let’s eat and drink, because tomorrow we die!”
The LORD of Armies told me himself, right in my ears, “You won’t be forgiven for this wrong as long as you live,” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The Lord, GOD of Armies, says, “Go find Shebna, that treasurer in charge of the household. Tell him,
‘What are you doing here? Who gave you a place here to dig yourself a tomb?’ Look at him cutting a tomb for himself up high, chiseling out a place for himself in the rock!”
Look, the LORD will get the better of you and hurl you away. He’ll grab you tight.
He’ll wrap you round and round and toss you like a ball into a wide-open land. You’ll die there, and your fancy chariots will end up there too. You’re a disgrace to your master’s household.
I’ll kick you out of office. You’ll be pulled down from your position.
That day I’ll call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I’ll dress him in your robe and tie your sash around him. I’ll put him in charge of what you used to govern, and he’ll be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and the house of Judah.
I’ll put the key to David’s house on his shoulder. What he opens, nobody will shut. What he shuts, nobody will open.
I’ll drive him in like a peg where it’ll hold fast. He’ll become a seat of honor for his father’s family.
They’ll hang all the honor of his father’s family on him, his children and their children, every little vessel from cups to pitchers.
“On that day,” says the LORD of Armies, “the peg fixed so firmly will give way. It’ll be cut down and fall. The load hanging on it will be cut off.” The LORD has spoken.
Here’s the warning for Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish! Tyre’s wrecked. There’s no house left and no way in. They hear the news from the land of Kittim.
Go quiet, you who live along the coast, you who were supplied by Sidon’s merchants who crossed the sea.
Across great waters came Shihor’s grain, the Nile’s harvest, and it brought in money for Tyre. She was the marketplace for nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon. The sea, the fortress of the sea, has spoken: “I haven’t been in labor or given birth. I haven’t raised young men or brought up young women.”
When the news reaches Egypt, people there will be in anguish over what happened to Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, you who live along the coast!
Is this your party city, the ancient one that went so far from home on her own feet?
Who planned this against Tyre, the one who handed out crowns? Her merchants were princes, and her traders were the respected people of the earth.
The LORD of Armies planned it to spoil the pride of all that glory and bring down the reputation of everyone the earth looks up to.
Flow across your land like the Nile, Daughter Tarshish. There’s nothing holding you back anymore.
He stretched his hand out over the sea and shook kingdoms. The LORD ordered Canaan’s strongholds destroyed.
He said, “Your celebrations are over, oppressed virgin Daughter Sidon. Get up and cross over to Kittim. You won’t get any rest there either.”
Look at the land of the Chaldeans. That people didn’t exist before. The Assyrians founded it for people of the wilderness. They put up siege towers, tore down its palaces, and left it in ruins.
Wail, ships of Tarshish! Your stronghold has been wrecked.
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the length of one king’s days. After seventy years, it’ll be like the song about the prostitute:
Grab a harp and walk around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play a sweet tune and sing lots of songs so somebody remembers you.
After those seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre. She’ll go back to earning her wages and play the prostitute with every kingdom on earth.

Her trade and what she earns will be set apart for the LORD. The money won’t be hoarded or stored. What she earns will go to the people who live before the LORD, so they have plenty to eat and clothes that last.
Look, the LORD is emptying the earth and laying it waste. He’s flipping it upside down and scattering everyone who lives on it.
It’ll be the same for people and priests, servants and masters, maids and mistresses, buyers and sellers, creditors and debtors, and people who charge interest and people who pay it.
The earth will be emptied out completely, utterly wrecked. The LORD said it.
The earth grieves and fades. The world withers and fades. Even the most important people on earth are wasting away.
The people living on earth have polluted it. They crossed the line with its laws, ignored its rules, and broke the covenant that was supposed to last forever.
So the curse has eaten up the earth, and its people are guilty. The people of earth are burned up, and barely anyone is left.
The new wine mourns. The vine is dying. Everybody who used to have a good time is left sighing.
The tambourines go quiet, the cheering dies out, and the harp’s happy tune stops.
Nobody sings over their wine now. Strong drink tastes bitter to the people drinking it.
The city is a wreck. Every house is shut tight so nobody can get in.
People cry in the streets for wine. All their joy has gone dark. All the good times have drained out of the land.
The city is left deserted, and its gate is smashed to pieces.
That’s how it’ll be among the peoples of the earth, like an olive tree after it’s been shaken, like the few grapes left after harvest.
The ones left will raise their voices and shout about the LORD’s majesty. They’ll cry out from the sea.
So honor the LORD in the east! Honor the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, on the islands out at sea!

From the far edge of the earth we’ve heard singing: “Glory to the righteous one!” But I said, “I’m wasting away! I’m wasting away! I’m done for!” Traitors have betrayed people, and their betrayal runs deep.
Terror, the pit, and the trap are waiting for you who live on earth.
Whoever runs from the sound of terror will fall in the pit. Whoever climbs out of the pit will get caught in the trap. The windows up above are open, and the earth’s foundations are shaking.
The earth is smashed apart. The earth is split open. The earth shakes hard.
The earth will stagger like someone who’s drunk and swing back and forth like a hammock. Its rebellion will weigh it down so heavily that it’ll fall and never get back up.
That day the LORD will punish the army of the high ones up above and the kings of the earth down here.
They’ll be rounded up like prisoners in a pit and locked away. After many days, they’ll be dealt with.
Then the moon will be embarrassed and the sun put to shame, because the LORD of Armies will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. His glory will shine before his elders.
LORD, you’re my God. I’ll lift you up and praise your name! You’ve done wonderful things you planned long ago, and you’ve been completely faithful and true.
You turned a city into a pile of rubble, a fortified city into ruins. That palace of foreigners is a city no longer. It’ll never be rebuilt.
That’s why a strong people will give you glory and the city of terrifying nations will stand in awe of you.
You’ve been a fortress for the poor, a shelter for people in desperate need, a refuge from the storm, and shade from the heat when ruthless people blast against the wall like a storm.
You quiet the uproar of foreigners like heat dying down in a dry place. Like a cloud cooling the heat with its shade, you hush the song of the ruthless.
On this mountain the LORD of Armies will lay out a feast for all peoples: the best meats, the best wines, rich meat full of marrow, and fine wines cleared of their sediment.
On this mountain he’ll destroy the covering spread over every people, the veil stretched over every nation.
He’s swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe tears off every face. He’ll take away the shame of his people from the whole earth. The LORD has spoken.
On that day people will say, “Look, this is our God! We waited for him, and he’ll save us! This is the LORD. We waited for him. Let’s be glad and celebrate the way he saves us!”
The LORD’s hand will rest on this mountain. Moab will be trampled where it stands, like straw stomped down in the muck of a manure pit.
Moab will stretch out its hands in the middle of it like a swimmer stretching out to swim, but its pride will come down along with all the clever work of its hands.
He’s brought your high, fortified walls down, leveled them all the way to the ground, right into the dust.
On that day people in Judah will sing this song: “We’ve got a strong city! God makes his rescue its walls and defenses.
Open the gates! Let the nation that does right come in, the one that stays faithful.
You’ll keep the one whose mind stays steady in perfect peace, because that person trusts you.
Trust the LORD forever. The LORD, the LORD himself, is a Rock that will always stand.
He’s brought down the ones living high above everyone else, that towering city. He brings it down, all the way to the ground, all the way to the dust.
Now feet will trample it, the feet of the poor and the steps of the needy.”
The road of those who do right is straight. You do what’s right, and you level the path for righteous people.
Yes, LORD, we’ve waited for you on the path of your judgments. Your name and your reputation are what we want with all our hearts.
I long for you with all my soul in the night. Deep in my spirit, I’ll seek you with everything I’ve got. When your judgments come on the earth, people in the world learn how to do what’s right.
Even when wicked people are shown kindness, they don’t learn to do right. In a land where people live honestly, they still do wrong and miss the LORD’s majesty.
LORD, your hand is raised, and they still don’t see it. But they’ll see how fiercely you stand up for your people, and they’ll be put to shame. Fire will swallow up your enemies.
LORD, you’ll establish peace for us, because you’re the one who has done all our work for us.
LORD our God, other masters have ruled over us, but yours is the only name we’ll honor.
Those dead won’t live again. Those departed spirits won’t rise. You came against them and destroyed them, and you wiped out every memory of them.
LORD, you’ve grown the nation. You’ve grown the nation! You get the glory! You’ve stretched out every border of the land.
LORD, when trouble hit, they came to you. When you disciplined them, they poured out a prayer.
Like a pregnant woman about to give birth who cries out in pain, that’s how we’ve been before you, LORD.
We were pregnant. We went through the pain. All we seem to have given birth to is wind. We haven’t brought rescue to the earth, and the people of the world haven’t fallen.
Your dead will live. Their bodies will rise. Wake up and sing, you who live in the dust! Your dew is like dew on fresh plants, and the earth will bring out the spirits of the dead.
Come, my people. Go into your rooms and close the doors behind you. Hide for a little while until the anger has passed.
Look, the LORD is coming out from where he lives to punish the earth’s people for what they’ve done wrong. The earth will expose the blood spilled on it and stop covering those who were killed.
On that day the LORD will use his hard, great, powerful sword to punish Leviathan, the fleeing snake, and Leviathan, the twisting snake. He’ll kill the dragon in the sea.
On that day, sing about her: “What a lovely vineyard!
I, the LORD, look after it. I water it all the time. I guard it night and day so nobody can hurt it.
I’m carrying no anger. But if I find briars and thorns, I’ll go to battle! I’ll march straight at them and burn them all.
Or they can take hold of my strength and make peace with me. Let them make peace with me.”
In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and bloom. They’ll fill the whole world with fruit.
Did he strike them like he struck the ones who hit them? Were they killed the way their killers were killed?
You dealt with them in measure when you sent them away. He drove them out with a hard blast the day the east wind blew.

That’s how Jacob’s wrongdoing will be forgiven. Here’s the full result of taking away his sin: he’ll smash every altar stone into bits like crushed chalk, and the Asherah poles and incense altars won’t stand again.
The fortified city stands alone, abandoned and empty like a wilderness. A calf will graze and lie down there, eating its branches.

When the branches dry out, they’ll snap off. Women will come and set them on fire. These people have no understanding. That’s why the one who made them won’t have compassion on them, and the one who formed them won’t show them favor.
On that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt. You’ll be gathered one by one, children of Israel.
On that day a great trumpet will blow. People close to dying in Assyria and people driven out to Egypt will come. They’ll worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Trouble’s coming for that proud crown worn by Ephraim’s drunks, that fading flower they brag about, perched above the fertile valley of people knocked out by wine!
Look, the Lord has someone powerful and strong. Like a hailstorm, a storm that wrecks everything, like a flood bursting over its banks, he’ll throw them to the ground with his hand.
That proud crown worn by Ephraim’s drunks will get stomped underfoot.
The fading flower of Ephraim’s glamorous beauty above the fertile valley will be like the first ripe fig before summer. Someone spots it, grabs it, and eats it on the spot.
On that day the LORD of Armies will be a glorious crown and a beautiful headpiece for those of his people who are left.
He’ll give a spirit of justice to the one sitting in judgment and strength to those who drive the fight back at the gate.

These people stagger from wine and wobble from hard drink. Priest and prophet both reel from strong drink. Wine has swallowed them up. They stagger from the liquor, get their visions wrong, and stumble when they give a ruling.
There’s filthy vomit covering every table. The whole place is a mess.
Who’s he going to teach? Who’s he explaining the message to? Kids who just stopped nursing?
It’s rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there.
But he’ll talk to this nation through stammering lips and in another language.
He told them, “Here’s where you can rest. Let the tired people rest. Here’s where you can catch your breath.” But they wouldn’t listen.

So the LORD’s word will sound like this to them: rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there. They’ll go, fall backward, get broken, get trapped, and be taken.
So hear the LORD’s word, you mockers running things here in Jerusalem.

“You said, ‘We made a deal with death and came to an agreement with Sheol. When that punishment comes flooding through, it won’t reach us. We’ve made lies our shelter and hid ourselves behind falsehood.’”
So the Lord GOD says, “Look, I’m laying a foundation stone in Zion. It’s been tested. It’s a precious cornerstone for a solid foundation. The person who trusts won’t rush in panic.
I’ll use justice as the measuring line and righteousness as the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the shelter you made out of lies, and floodwaters will wash over your hiding place.
Your deal with death will be canceled. Your agreement with Sheol won’t hold. When that punishment comes flooding through, it’ll trample you.
Every time it sweeps through, it’ll grab you. Morning after morning, all day and all night, it’ll come through. Finally understanding the message will be pure terror.”
The bed’s too short to stretch out on, and the blanket’s too narrow to wrap around you.
The LORD will rise up like he did on Mount Perazim. He’ll get angry like he did in the Valley of Gibeon. He’ll do his work, his unusual work, and carry out his act, his extraordinary act.
So quit mocking, or your chains will be tightened. I’ve heard a decree of destruction over the whole earth from the Lord, GOD of Armies.
Give me your ear and hear my voice! Listen to what I’m saying!
Does a farmer plow forever when he’s trying to sow? Does he go on turning dirt and breaking up clumps?
Once he’s leveled the ground, doesn’t he sow dill and scatter cumin seed, line up the wheat in rows, and put the barley and spelt where they belong?
His God shows him the right way and teaches him.
You don’t run a sharp threshing tool over dill or roll a cartwheel over cumin. You beat the dill out with a stick and the cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread has to be ground, but the farmer doesn’t thresh it forever. He rolls the wheel of his threshing cart over it, but his horses don’t grind it up.
This comes from the LORD of Armies too. His advice is wonderful, and his wisdom is outstanding.
Trouble is coming for Ariel! Ariel, the city where David made camp. Go on, add another year, let the festivals come around again.
Then I’ll bring distress on Ariel. There’ll be crying and mourning, and she’ll be like an altar hearth to me.
I’ll camp against you on every side. I’ll post troops around you and build siege works against you.

You’ll be brought low, talking out of the ground. Your words will come mumbling up out of the dust. Your voice will sound like someone speaking through a spirit from the ground. You’ll whisper from the dust.
But your many enemies will be like fine dust, and the crowds of ruthless people like chaff blowing away. It’ll happen fast, in an instant.
The LORD of Armies will come to her with thunder, earthquakes, a massive roar, whirlwinds, storms, and flames that eat everything up.
The armies of all the nations fighting Ariel, everyone attacking her and her stronghold and bringing her trouble, will be like a dream in the middle of the night.

It’ll be like a hungry person dreaming they’re eating, then waking up just as hungry. Or like a thirsty person dreaming they’re drinking, then waking up weak and still thirsty. That’s how it’ll be for all those nations fighting Mount Zion.
Stop and be shocked! Blind yourselves and go blind! They’re drunk without wine, staggering without strong drink.
The LORD has poured a spirit of deep sleep on you. He’s shut your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.
The whole vision is like the words in a sealed book. Someone hands it to a person who can read and says, “Read this, please.” They say, “I can’t. It’s sealed.”
Then someone hands the book to a person who can’t read and says, “Read this, please.” They say, “I don’t know how to read.”

The Lord said, “These people come close to me with their words and honor me with their lips, but they’ve pulled their hearts far away from me. The respect they show me is just a human rule they were taught.
So watch. I’m going to do something incredible with these people, wonder after wonder. The wisdom of their wise will disappear, and the understanding of the clever will be hidden.”
Trouble is coming for people who bury their plans where they think the LORD can’t find them, who do their deeds in the dark and say, “Who sees us? Who knows what we’re doing?”
You’ve got it all upside down! Is the potter just like the clay? Can something that was made say about its maker, “He didn’t make me”? Can the thing he shaped say about him, “He has no clue”?
Won’t it be just a little while before Lebanon turns into a fruitful field and the fruitful field gets called a forest?
On that day deaf people will hear the words of the book. Blind eyes will see out of the gloom and darkness.
The humble will find more and more joy in the LORD, and the poorest people will celebrate in the Holy One of Israel.
The ruthless will come to nothing, the mocker will be gone, and everyone on the lookout for a chance to do evil will be cut off.
That means people who use a word to get someone charged, set traps for anyone who calls out wrongdoing at the city gate, and lie in court to cheat innocent people out of justice.
So the LORD who rescued Abraham says this about Jacob’s family: “Jacob won’t have to hang his head anymore, and his face won’t go pale.
When he sees his children there with him, the work of my hands, they’ll honor my name as holy. They’ll honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
People who were lost in spirit will come to understand, and people who used to grumble will take instruction.”
“Trouble’s coming for those rebellious children,” says the LORD. “They make plans without asking me. They make an alliance without my Spirit and pile sin on top of sin.
They head down to Egypt without asking my advice, hoping Pharaoh’s power will make them strong and Egypt’s shadow will keep them safe.
So Pharaoh’s power will leave you ashamed, and trying to hide in Egypt’s shadow will leave you confused.
Your officials are already in Zoan, and your envoys have reached Hanes.
All of them will be ashamed because that nation can’t do a thing for them. No help, no gain, just shame and disgrace.”

Here’s the warning about the animals of the South. Through a land of trouble and anguish, of lionesses and lions, vipers and fiery flying snakes, they haul their riches on young donkeys’ backs and their treasures on camel humps to a people who can’t help them.
Egypt’s help is pointless. It gets you nowhere. So I call her Rahab Who Sits Still.
Now go write this on a tablet in front of them. Put it in a book so it’s there for all the days to come, forever.
These are rebellious people, children who lie, children who refuse to listen to the LORD’s teaching.
They tell the seers, “Don’t see!” And they tell the prophets, “Stop telling us what’s right. Tell us what sounds good. Give us prophecies that lie to us.
Get out of the way! Step off the path! Get the Holy One of Israel out of our faces.”
So the Holy One of Israel says, “You’ve treated this word with contempt, put your trust in oppression and dishonesty, and leaned on them.
So this wrong will be like a crack bulging out in a high wall that’s about to collapse. It’ll come crashing down in an instant.
He’ll smash it like a clay pot, breaking it without holding back. There won’t be a piece big enough to scoop a coal from the fire or dip up water from the cistern.”
The Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, said, “Come back and rest, and you’ll be saved. Your strength will come from staying calm and trusting.” But you wouldn’t do it.
You said, “No, we’ll get away on horses!” So you’ll run. “We’ll ride fast ones!” Then the people coming after you will be fast too.
A thousand of you will run when one person threatens you. When five do, you’ll scatter till you’re left like a lone signal pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.
Even so, the LORD will wait so he can show you grace. He’ll rise up to have mercy on you. The LORD is a God of justice. Everyone who waits for him is blessed.
People will live in Zion, in Jerusalem. You won’t have to cry anymore. The sound of your cry will move him to show you grace. When he hears you, he’ll answer you.
The Lord may feed you the bread of hardship and give you the water of suffering, but your teachers won’t stay hidden. You’ll see them with your own eyes.
If you turn right or left, you’ll hear a voice behind you saying, “Here’s the way. Walk in it.”
You’ll make the silver covering on your carved idols and the gold plating on your cast idols unclean. You’ll throw them out like something filthy and say, “Get out of here!”
He’ll send rain for the seed you plant in the ground. The land will produce plenty of rich bread. On that day your livestock will graze in wide-open pastures.
The oxen and young donkeys that work the soil will eat good feed, sifted clean with shovel and fork.
Brooks and streams will flow on every high mountain and tall hill on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers come down.

The moon will be as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like seven days’ worth of light. That’s the day the LORD will bind up his people’s broken bones and heal the wound he struck them with.
Look, the LORD’s name is coming from far away, burning with anger and trailing thick smoke. His lips are full of rage. His tongue is like a fire that eats everything up.
His breath is like a flood that reaches up to the neck. He’ll shake the nations in a sieve that destroys them. A bridle in the jaws of the peoples will steer them to ruin.
You’ll sing like you do at night during a holy feast. Your heart will be glad like someone walking with a flute to the LORD’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
The LORD will make his glorious voice heard. He’ll let people see his arm come down in furious anger, with flames that devour, with a blast, a storm, and hailstones.
The LORD’s voice will terrify the Assyrian. He’ll strike him with his rod.
Every blow the LORD lands with his rod of punishment will come to the sound of tambourines and harps. He’ll fight them in battle, swinging his weapons.
His burning place has been ready a long time. Yes, it’s set up for the king. He’s made the pyre wide and deep, full of fire and wood. The LORD’s breath sets it alight like a stream of sulfur.

Trouble is coming for those who go down to Egypt for help. They lean on horses and trust in chariots because there are so many and in riders because they’re so strong. They never look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD.
But he’s wise too. He’ll bring disaster and won’t take back what he said. He’ll rise up against the household of evildoers and against anyone who helps those who do wrong.

Egyptians are human. They aren’t God. Their horses are flesh and blood, with no power of spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble, the one getting help will fall, and they’ll both be wiped out together.

The LORD told me, “Think of a lion or a young lion growling over its prey. Get a whole crowd of shepherds shouting at it, and their voices won’t scare it or make it back down. That’s how the LORD of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and its heights.
Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD of Armies will guard Jerusalem. He’ll protect and rescue it. He’ll pass over it and keep it safe.”
Children of Israel, come back to the one you’ve rebelled against so deeply.
That day everyone will throw away their silver and gold idols, the sin their own hands made.
“The Assyrian will fall by a sword no human swings. A sword from no human hand will devour him. He’ll run from the sword, and his young men will be forced to work.
His rock will give way in terror, and his officers will panic at the sight of the banner,” says the LORD, whose fire burns in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, a king will reign doing what’s right, and his officials will rule with justice.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind, a hiding place from the storm, streams in a dry place, or a huge rock throwing shade in a worn-out land.
The eyes of those who see won’t be dim, and people with ears to hear will actually listen.
People who rush in without thinking will come to understand, and people who stammer will be ready to speak clearly.
Nobody will call the fool noble anymore, and nobody will treat the cheat like someone worth looking up to.
The fool talks nonsense and plans wrong in his heart. He treats holy things with contempt, says false things about the LORD, leaves hungry people empty, and keeps thirsty people from getting a drink.
The cheat’s methods are rotten. He makes wicked plans to ruin humble people with lies, even when someone in need is telling the truth.
But people of honor make honorable plans, and they stick with what’s honorable.
Get up, you women taking it easy! Hear my voice! You daughters without a care, listen to what I’m saying!
In a little over a year, you carefree women will be shaken. The grapes will fail. The harvest won’t come.
Shake, you women taking it easy! Be troubled, you carefree ones! Strip down and tie sackcloth around your waist.
Beat your chests for those beautiful fields and the vines that used to be full of fruit.
Thorns and briars will push up on my people’s land. Yes, they’ll cover every house that used to be full of laughter in that happy city.
The palace will be abandoned. The bustling city will empty out. The hill and watchtower will become dens forever, a happy place for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks,
until the Spirit is poured out on us from above. Then the wilderness will become a fruitful field, and people will call that fruitful field a forest.
Justice will live in the wilderness, and righteousness will stay in the fruitful field.
Doing what’s right will produce peace, and the result of righteousness will be quiet and confidence forever.
