My people will live where there’s peace, in safe homes and quiet spots to rest,
even when hail flattens the forest and the city is leveled to the ground.
Blessed are you who sow beside every stream and let the ox and donkey go out freely.

Trouble’s coming for you, destroyer. Nobody destroyed you. You betrayed people, and nobody betrayed you. Once you’re done destroying, you’ll be destroyed. Once you’re done betraying, you’ll be betrayed.
LORD, show us grace. We’ve waited for you. Be our strength every morning and rescue us when trouble hits.
At the roar of the thunder, peoples scattered. When you rose up, the nations ran.
Your loot will be picked clean like caterpillars picking a field clean. People will swarm over it like locusts.
The LORD is high above everything, because he lives on high. He’s filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your days will be steady, full of rescue, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is your treasure.
Look, their bravest people are crying out in the streets. The messengers of peace are weeping bitterly.
The highways are empty. Nobody travels anymore. He broke the agreement, treated cities with contempt, and showed no regard for anybody.
The land mourns and wastes away. Lebanon is disgraced and withers. Sharon turns into a desert. Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.
“Now I’ll get up,” says the LORD. “Now I’ll rise. Now I’ll be lifted high.
You’ll conceive chaff and give birth to stubble. Your own breath is a fire that’ll eat you up.
The peoples will burn like lime in a kiln, like thorns cut down and set on fire.
You far away, hear what I did. You close by, acknowledge how mighty I am.”
The sinners in Zion are scared. Shaking has taken hold of the godless. Who among us can live with a fire that eats everything up? Who can live with flames that never die?

The person who lives right and speaks honestly, who wants nothing to do with money squeezed out of people, who waves off a bribe, covers their ears at talk of bloodshed, and closes their eyes to evil,
that’s the person who’ll live high up. A rocky stronghold will keep them safe. They’ll have bread to eat and water they can count on.
Your eyes will see the king in all his beauty. They’ll see a land far away.
You’ll think back on the terror. Where’s the one who did the counting? Where’s the one who did the weighing? Where’s the one who counted the towers?
You won’t have to see those fierce people anymore, the ones who spoke in words you couldn’t make out, in a language you couldn’t understand.
Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. You’ll see Jerusalem, a quiet home, a tent that won’t be moved. Its stakes will never come out, and none of its ropes will snap.
The LORD will be there with us in his majesty. It’ll be a place of broad rivers and streams, where no ship with oars and no grand sailing ship will pass.
The LORD is our judge. The LORD gives us our laws. The LORD is our king. He’ll save us.
Your ropes hang loose. They couldn’t secure the foot of the mast or spread the sail. Then people split up a huge haul of loot. Even people who couldn’t walk took a share.
Nobody living there will say, “I’m sick.” The people living there will be forgiven for the wrong they’ve done.
Come close and listen, you nations! Pay attention, you peoples. Let the earth and everything in it hear, the whole world and everything that comes from it.
The LORD is furious with every nation and angry with all their armies. He’s destroyed them completely and handed them over to be slaughtered.
Their dead will be thrown out, and the stench from their bodies will rise. The mountains will melt in their blood.
The whole army of the sky will dissolve. The sky will roll up like a scroll, and all its armies will wither like leaves falling from a vine or a fig tree.
My sword has had its fill in the sky. Look, it’s coming down on Edom, on the people I’ve cursed, to bring judgment.
The LORD’s sword is full of blood and covered in fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with fat from the rams’ kidneys. The LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in Edom’s land.
Wild oxen will go down with them, young bulls along with powerful bulls. Their land will drink itself drunk on blood, and fat will soak the dust.
The LORD has a day for vengeance, a year to settle accounts for Zion’s sake.
Its streams will turn into pitch, its dust into sulfur, and the land itself will become burning pitch.
It won’t go out, day or night. Its smoke will keep rising forever. Generation after generation it’ll lie empty, and nobody will ever pass through again.
Pelicans and porcupines will take it over. Owls and ravens will live there. He’ll stretch a measuring line of chaos across it and drop a plumb line of emptiness.
They’ll call the nobles to take up the kingdom, and nobody will be there. All its officials will amount to nothing.
Thorns will grow up inside its palaces, nettles and thistles inside its fortresses. Jackals will call it home, and ostriches will fill its courtyards.
Desert animals will meet wolves there, and wild goats will call to each other. The night creature will settle in and find somewhere to rest.
The arrow snake will nest there, lay and hatch her eggs, and gather her young under her shade. The kites will gather there too, each with its mate.
Look it up in the LORD’s book and read it. Every one of these will be there. Each one will have its mate. My mouth gave the command, and his Spirit gathered them.
He drew lots for them and marked out their shares with his own hand and a measuring line. They’ll own it forever. They’ll live there from generation to generation.
The wilderness and dry land will be glad. The desert will celebrate and bloom like a rose.

Flowers will burst out everywhere, and the desert will sing for joy. It’ll be given the splendor of Lebanon and the beauty of Carmel and Sharon. They’ll see the LORD’s glory and the greatness of our God.
Strengthen hands that have gone weak. Steady knees that keep giving way.
Tell people whose hearts are full of fear, “Stand strong! Don’t be afraid! Look, your God is coming to set things right and bring retribution. He’s coming to save you.
Then blind eyes will open, and deaf ears will hear.
Then the person who couldn’t walk will leap like a deer, and the person who couldn’t speak will sing. Water will burst out in the wilderness and streams will run through the desert.
Burning sand will turn into a pool, and thirsty ground into springs of water. Where jackals used to lie down, grass, reeds, and rushes will grow.
There’ll be a highway called the Holy Way. People who are unclean won’t cross it. It’s for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools won’t go there.
There won’t be a lion on that road. No hungry beast will come up there or be found there. The redeemed will walk there.
Then the people the LORD ransomed will come back. They’ll come singing to Zion, crowned with joy that lasts forever. Gladness and joy will be theirs, and grief and sighing will run away.”
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah’s reign, King Sennacherib of Assyria attacked all Judah’s fortified cities and took them.

The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem with a huge army. Rabshakeh stood by the water channel from the upper pool on the road to the field where cloth was washed.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who ran the royal household, went out to meet him, along with Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
Rabshakeh told them, “Tell Hezekiah this: ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What are you banking on so hard?
I say your plans and strength for war are nothing but talk. Who are you trusting now that you’ve rebelled against me?
Look at Egypt, that cracked reed you’re using as a walking stick. Lean on it and it’ll go straight through your hand. That’s what Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, is like to everyone who trusts him.
But if you tell me, ‘We trust the LORD our God,’ isn’t that the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah took away? Didn’t Hezekiah tell Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Worship in front of this altar’?”
Come on, make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I’ll give you two thousand horses, if you’ve even got enough people to ride them.
How are you going to drive back even the least captain my master has while you’re counting on Egypt for chariots and riders?
You think I came to wreck this land without the LORD? The LORD told me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’”
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to us, your servants, in Aramaic. We understand it. Don’t speak in the Judeans’ language where the people on the wall can hear you.”

Rabshakeh replied, “You think my master sent me with this message just for you and your master? What about the men sitting on that wall who’ll have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine right alongside you?”
Then Rabshakeh stood and shouted in the Judeans’ language, “Hear what the great king, the king of Assyria, has to say!
The king says, ‘Don’t let Hezekiah fool you. He won’t be able to save you.
Don’t let Hezekiah talk you into trusting the LORD by saying, “The LORD will definitely save us. This city won’t fall into the hands of the king of Assyria.”’
Don’t listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, ‘Make peace with me and come out to me. Each of you can eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink water from your own cistern,
until I come and take you to a land like yours, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Watch out for Hezekiah talking you into believing the LORD will save you. Have any of the gods of the nations saved their lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?
Which god of any of these lands has rescued its country from me? So what makes you think the LORD will rescue Jerusalem from me?’”
They stayed quiet and didn’t say a thing back. The king had ordered, “Don’t answer him.”
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who ran the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him what Rabshakeh said.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the LORD’s house.
He sent Eliakim, the head of the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. They were all wearing sackcloth.
They told him, “Hezekiah says, ‘Today is a day of trouble, rebuke, and rejection. It’s like a baby ready to be born when there’s no strength left to give birth.

Maybe the LORD your God will hear what Rabshakeh said. His master, the king of Assyria, sent him to defy the living God. Maybe the LORD your God will rebuke him for what he heard him say. Please pray for the few of us still left.’”
So King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah.
Isaiah told them, “Tell your master this: ‘The LORD says, “Don’t be afraid of what you heard, all that talk from the king of Assyria’s servants insulting me.
Look, I’ll put a spirit in him. He’ll hear some news and go back to his own land. I’ll make him fall by the sword there in his own country.”’”
Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, so he went back and found him fighting against Libnah.
Then the king heard news about King Tirhakah of Ethiopia: “He’s come out to fight you.” When he heard that, he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
“Tell King Hezekiah of Judah, ‘Don’t let that God you trust fool you by saying Jerusalem won’t fall into the king of Assyria’s hands.
You’ve heard what Assyria’s kings did to every land they destroyed completely. You think you’ll get away?
Did the gods of the nations save the people my fathers wiped out, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who lived in Telassar?
Where’s the king of Hamath? Where’s the king of Arpad? Where’s the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD’s house and spread it out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
“LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you sit on your throne among the cherubim. You alone are God over every kingdom on earth. You made heaven and earth.
Turn your ear this way, LORD, and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and look. Hear every word Sennacherib sent to defy the living God.
It’s true, LORD. The kings of Assyria destroyed those countries and their lands.
They threw their gods into the fire. Those things were wood and stone somebody made by hand. They weren’t gods, and that’s how Assyria could destroy them.
So now, LORD our God, save us from him so every kingdom on earth knows that you alone are the LORD.”
Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “The LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘You prayed to me about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
Here’s what the LORD says about him. Virgin Daughter Zion looks down on you and laughs at you. Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
Who have you defied and insulted? Who’d you raise your voice against? Who did you lift your eyes against? The Holy One of Israel.

You used your servants to defy the Lord. You said, “With all my chariots, I climbed to the mountaintops, deep into Lebanon. I’ll cut down its tall cedars and the best cypresses. I’ll push up to its farthest heights, into the forest of its richest land.
I dug and drank water, and with the soles of my feet I’ll dry up every river in Egypt.”
“‘Haven’t you heard? I did this long ago. I planned it way back. Now I’ve made it happen: you’re the one turning fortified cities into piles of rubble.
That’s why the people who lived there had no strength. They were terrified and confused, like grass in a field, like green plants, like grass on a rooftop, like a field before the crop comes up.
I know when you sit down, when you head out, when you come back, and when you rage at me.
Because you raged at me and I heard all your arrogant talk, I’ll put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I’ll turn you around and send you back the way you came.
“‘Here’s the sign for you. This year you’ll eat what grows on its own, and next year what springs up from that. In the third year, sow and harvest, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The survivors of Judah will put down roots again and bear fruit above.
A remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The passion of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.’
“So here’s what the LORD says about Assyria’s king: ‘He won’t come into this city or shoot an arrow here. He won’t march up with a shield or pile up a siege ramp against it.
He’ll go back the way he came. He won’t enter this city,’ says the LORD.
‘I’ll defend this city and save it for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.’”
Then the LORD’s angel went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When people got up early the next morning, there were dead bodies everywhere.
So King Sennacherib of Assyria broke camp, went back to Nineveh, and stayed there.
While he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esar Haddon became king in his place.
Around then Hezekiah got sick and was close to death. Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said, “The LORD says, ‘Get your house in order. You’re going to die. You won’t recover.’”
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
“LORD, please remember how I’ve lived faithfully before you with my whole heart and done what’s good in your eyes.” Then Hezekiah broke down and cried.
Then the LORD spoke to Isaiah:
“Go tell Hezekiah, ‘The LORD, the God of your father David, says, “I’ve heard your prayer. I’ve seen your tears. Look, I’ll add fifteen years to your life.
I’ll rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria, and I’ll defend this city.
Here’s the sign from the LORD that he’ll do what he said.
Look, I’ll make the shadow that moved down Ahaz’s sundial with the sun go back up ten steps.”’” So the sun went back ten steps on the sundial where it had gone down.
Here’s what King Hezekiah of Judah wrote after he got sick and recovered:
I said, “In the middle of my life, I’m going through the gates of Sheol. The years I had left are being taken from me.”
I said, “I won’t see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living. I won’t see anybody among the people of this world again.
My home is taken down and carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I’ve rolled up my life like a weaver, and he’ll cut me off the loom. From day to night you’ll bring me to an end.
I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day to night you’ll bring me to an end.
I chirped like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes are wearing out from looking up. Lord, I’m being crushed. Stand up for me.”
What can I say? He spoke to me, and he did it himself. I’ll walk carefully all my years because of the anguish I felt deep down.
Lord, people live by these things. In all of them my spirit finds life. You restore me and give me life.
Look, instead of peace I had deep pain, but you loved me and pulled my life out of the pit of decay. You threw all my sins behind your back.
Sheol can’t praise you. Death can’t celebrate you. People who go down to the pit can’t hope in your truth.
The living, yes, the living praise you just like I do today. A father tells his children about your truth.
The LORD will save me. So we’ll sing my songs to stringed instruments every day of our lives in the LORD’s house.
Isaiah had said, “Get a cake of figs and put it on the boil as a poultice, and he’ll get better.”
Hezekiah had also asked, “What’s the sign that I’ll go up to the LORD’s house?”
Around then King Merodach-baladan of Babylon, son of Baladan, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah. He’d heard that Hezekiah got sick and recovered.

Hezekiah was happy to see them and showed them his treasure house. He showed them the silver, gold, spices, expensive oil, his whole armory, and every last thing in his storerooms. There wasn’t a thing in his house or anywhere he ruled that he kept from them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did those men say? Where did they come from?” Hezekiah said, “They came from a country far away from me, all the way from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked, “What did they see in your house?” Hezekiah answered, “They saw everything in my house. I didn’t leave a single treasure out.”
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear what the LORD of Armies says:
‘Look, the days are coming when everything in your house, everything your fathers stored up to this day, will be hauled off to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.
‘They’ll take away your sons, sons you yourself will father, and make them eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace.’”
Hezekiah told Isaiah, “The word you’ve spoken from the LORD is good.” He added, “There’ll be peace and truth in my days.”
“Comfort my people. Comfort them,” says your God.
“Speak gently to Jerusalem. Call out to her that her time of fighting is over, her wrongdoing is forgiven, and she’s received double from the LORD’s hand for all her sins.”
A voice calls out, “Get the LORD’s road ready in the wilderness! Make a level highway through the desert for our God.
Raise every valley and bring every mountain and hill down. Level the uneven ground and make the rough land a plain.
The LORD’s glory will be seen, and everyone will see it together. The LORD himself said it.”
A voice says, “Cry out!” Someone asks, “What should I cry out?” “Every human is like grass, and all their glory is like a flower in the field.
The grass dries up and the flower fades when the LORD’s breath blows over it. People really are like grass.
The grass dries up. The flower fades. Our God’s word stands forever.”
You bringing good news to Zion, get up on a high mountain! You bringing good news to Jerusalem, let your voice ring out! Lift it up! Don’t be afraid! Tell Judah’s towns, “Look, here’s your God!”
Look, the Lord GOD is coming with power. His own arm will rule for him. Look, he’s bringing his reward with him, and what he’ll give in return goes before him.
He’ll feed his flock like a shepherd. He’ll scoop up the lambs in his arm and hold them close to his chest. He’ll gently lead the ones caring for their young.
Who’s ever measured the waters in the palm of his hand, marked out the sky with the width of his hand, measured the earth’s dust in a basket, or weighed mountains and hills on a set of scales?
Who has told the LORD’s Spirit what to do? Who’s been his adviser and taught him anything?
Who did he go to for advice? Who instructed him, taught him how to judge justly, gave him knowledge, or showed him the way to understand?
Look, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, like a speck of dust on the scales. He lifts the islands like they barely weigh a thing.
All of Lebanon’s wood wouldn’t make enough fire, and all its animals wouldn’t be enough for a burnt offering.
Every nation counts for nothing before him. To him they’re less than nothing, all their greatness empty.
So who could you compare God to? What could you make that’s anything like him?
A worker casts a figure. A goldsmith covers it with gold and makes silver chains for it.
Someone who can’t afford that kind of offering picks wood that won’t rot and looks for a skilled worker to carve a figure that won’t tip over.
Don’t you know? Haven’t you heard? Hasn’t it been told to you from the start? Haven’t you understood since the earth was founded?
He’s the one seated above the circle of the earth. Its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them like a tent to live in.
He brings rulers to nothing and makes the earth’s judges count for nothing.
They’ve barely been planted, barely been sown. Their stems have barely put down roots. He breathes on them and they shrivel up, and a whirlwind sweeps them off like stubble.
“So who will you compare me to? Who’s my equal?” says the Holy One.
Look up and see. Who made all of these? He brings out their whole army, each one counted, and calls each one by name. He’s so mighty and so strong that every last one shows up.
Jacob, why do you say this? Israel, why are you saying, “The LORD can’t see what’s happening to me. My God is ignoring the justice I’m owed”?

Don’t you know? Haven’t you heard? The LORD is the God who’s always been there, the Creator of the farthest reaches of the earth. He doesn’t pass out or wear down. Nobody can get to the bottom of what he understands.
He gives strength to the weak. He gives more power to people who have none left.
Even young people get tired and collapse. Even strong young men fall hard.
But those who wait for the LORD will get their strength back. They’ll rise on wings like eagles. They’ll run without wearing out. They’ll walk without passing out. 🦅
“Quiet before me, you islands. Let the peoples get their strength back. Let them come close, and then let them speak. Let’s meet to settle this in judgment.

Who raised someone up from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands nations over to him and puts him over kings. Their armies become dust before his sword and windblown stubble before his bow.
He chases them and passes through safely, even on roads his feet have never walked.
Who’s done all this, calling each generation from the beginning? I have. I’m the LORD, the first, and I’m there with the last.”
The islands see it and get scared. The ends of the earth shake. They draw near and come together.
Everyone helps their neighbor and tells the person beside them, “Stay strong!”
The carpenter cheers on the goldsmith. The one smoothing the metal with a hammer encourages the one striking the anvil. They say, “That joint looks good!” Then they nail it down so it won’t wobble.
“But you, Israel, are my servant. You’re Jacob, the one I chose, descended from Abraham my friend.
I took hold of you from the ends of the earth, called you from its far corners, and told you, ‘You’re my servant. I chose you, and I haven’t thrown you away.’
Don’t be scared. I’m with you. Don’t lose heart. I’m your God. I’ll strengthen you. I’ll help you. I’ll hold you steady with my righteous right hand.
Look, everyone who’s furious with you will wind up ashamed and confused. The ones who fight you will amount to nothing and die out.
You’ll look for them, the ones who came against you, and you won’t find them. The people at war with you will be gone like they were never there.
I’m the LORD your God. I take hold of your right hand and say, ‘Don’t be afraid. I’ll help you.’
Don’t be afraid, little worm Jacob, you people of Israel. I’ll help you,” says the LORD. “The Holy One of Israel is the one who redeems you.
Look, I’ve made you into a brand-new threshing tool with sharp teeth. You’ll thresh the mountains, crush them down small, and turn the hills into chaff.
You’ll toss it all in the air. The wind will carry it off, and a whirlwind will scatter it. Then you’ll celebrate in the LORD and take pride in the Holy One of Israel.
Poor people in need look for water, and there’s none. Their tongues are drying up with thirst. I’m the LORD, and I’ll answer them. I’m the God of Israel, and I won’t leave them on their own.
I’ll open up rivers on bare heights and springs in the middle of valleys. I’ll turn wilderness into a pool and dry land into springs of water.
I’ll put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I’ll plant cypress, pine, and box trees together in the desert,
so everybody can see it, know it, think it over, and understand that the LORD’s hand did it. The Holy One of Israel created it.
Make your case,” says the LORD. “Bring your strongest arguments,” says Jacob’s King.
“Let them come tell us what’s going to happen. Tell us what happened before, so we can think it over and see how it ended. Or show us what’s coming next.
Tell us what happens after this so we’ll know you’re gods. Go ahead, do something good or bad, so we can all see it and be shaken.
Look at you. You’re nothing, and what you do is nothing. The person who chooses you is detestable.
“I raised someone up from the north, and he came. From the east comes someone who calls on my name. He’ll walk over rulers like mortar, like a potter stepping on clay.
Who told us this from the start so we could know? Who told us beforehand so we could say, ‘You got it right’? Nobody declared it. Nobody showed it. Nobody heard you say a word.
I was the first to tell Zion, ‘Look, there they are!’ And I’ll give Jerusalem someone to bring good news.
I look around and nobody’s there. There’s nobody among them who can give advice or even give me a word back when I ask.
Look, all their work comes to nothing. Their cast idols are wind and confusion.”
“Look at my servant. I hold him steady. I chose him, and he brings me deep joy. I’ve put my Spirit on him. He’ll bring justice to the nations.
He won’t shout, raise his voice, or make himself heard out in the streets.
He won’t snap a bruised reed or put out a wick that’s barely burning. He’ll faithfully bring justice.
He won’t give out or lose heart until he’s set justice in place on earth. The islands are waiting for his teaching.”

Here’s what God the LORD says, the one who made the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything that comes out of it, who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk on it:
“I’m the LORD. I’ve called you in righteousness. I’ll hold your hand and keep you safe. I’ll make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and free people sitting in the dark.
“I’m the LORD. That’s my name. I won’t give my glory to anyone else or hand my praise to carved idols.
Look, the things I said before have happened. Now I’m telling you new things. I’m letting you know before they even come up.”
Sing a new song to the LORD! Praise him from the far ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea and all that lives there, the islands and the people on them.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, along with the villages where Kedar lives. Let the people of Sela sing. Let them shout from the mountaintops!
Let them give the LORD glory and tell the islands how worthy he is of praise.
The LORD will go out like a mighty warrior. He’ll stir up his passion like someone ready for battle. He’ll give a war cry, loud and clear. He’ll win against his enemies.
“I’ve been quiet a long time. I kept still and held it all in. Now I’ll cry out like a woman in labor. I’ll gasp and pant.
I’ll wreck mountains and hills and dry out all their plants. I’ll turn rivers into islands and dry up the pools.

I’ll take blind people along a road they’ve never known. I’ll lead them down unfamiliar paths. I’ll turn the dark ahead of them into light and straighten the places that twist. I’ll do all this, and I won’t abandon them.
“People who trust carved figures and tell cast idols, ‘You’re our gods,’ will be turned back and left completely ashamed.
“Listen, you who are deaf! Look, you who are blind, so you can see.
Who’s blind like my servant? Who’s as deaf as the messenger I send? Who’s as blind as the one at peace with me, as blind as the LORD’s servant?
You see a lot, but you don’t pay attention. His ears are open, but he isn’t listening.”
For the sake of his righteousness, the LORD was glad to make his teaching great and honorable.

But these people have been robbed and stripped of everything. They’re all trapped in holes, hidden away in prisons. They’ve been taken captive with nobody to free them, hauled off like loot with nobody saying, “Give them back!”
Which one of you will pay attention to this? Who’ll listen and take it in for the days ahead?
Who handed Jacob over as loot and gave Israel to the robbers? Wasn’t it the LORD, the one we sinned against? They wouldn’t follow his ways and wouldn’t obey his teaching.
So he poured his fierce anger and the force of battle on them. It set them on fire all around, and they didn’t realize. It burned them, and they still didn’t take it to heart.
But now the LORD who made you, Jacob, the one who shaped you, Israel, says, “Don’t be afraid. I’ve redeemed you. I’ve called you by name. You’re mine.
When you go through deep waters, I’ll be there with you. The rivers won’t sweep over you. When you walk through fire, you won’t burn. The flames won’t scorch you.
I’m the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I gave Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
You’re precious to me, and I’ve honored you and loved you. So I’ll give people in your place, nations in exchange for your life.
Don’t be afraid. I’m with you. I’ll bring your children back from the east and gather you in from the west.
I’ll tell the north, ‘Hand them over!’ and the south, ‘Don’t hold them back! Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
Bring everyone called by my name, everyone I created for my glory, everyone I shaped and made.’”
Bring out the blind people who have eyes and the deaf people who have ears.

Let all the nations come together. Let the peoples gather. Which of them can declare this and show us what happened before? Let them bring witnesses to prove their case, or let them listen and say, “That’s true.”
“You’re my witnesses,” says the LORD, “along with the servant I chose, so you can know me, believe me, and understand that I am he. No god was formed before me, and none will come after me.
I myself am the LORD. There’s no savior besides me.
I told you, I saved you, and I made it known. There was no foreign god among you. So you’re my witnesses,” says the LORD, “and I’m God.
Yes, from the first day, I am he. Nobody can snatch anyone out of my hand. When I act, who can stop me?”
The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says, “For your sake I’ve sent to Babylon. I’ll bring its people down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans in the ships they were so proud of.
I’m the LORD, your Holy One, the one who created Israel, your King.”
The LORD makes a road through the sea and a path through mighty waters.
He draws out the chariot and horse, the army and the warrior. Down they go together, never to get up. They go out like a wick. Here’s what he says:
“Quit dwelling on the past. Don’t keep going back over what happened long ago.
Look! I’m doing something new. It’s springing up right now. Can’t you see it? I’ll make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
Wild animals will honor me, the jackals and ostriches, because I put water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert so my chosen people can drink.
I formed these people for myself so they’d speak my praise.
But you didn’t call on me, Jacob. You got tired of me, Israel.
You didn’t bring me sheep for burnt offerings or honor me with sacrifices. I didn’t weigh you down with offerings or wear you out asking for frankincense.
You didn’t spend money on sweet cane for me or satisfy me with the fat of your sacrifices. You loaded me down with your sins, though. You wore me out with your wrongdoing.
I’m the one who wipes away your rebellion for my own sake, and I won’t remember your sins.
Remind me. Let’s argue the case together. Tell your side so you can be shown to be in the right.
Your first father sinned, and the people who taught you rebelled against me.
So I’ll strip the leaders of the sanctuary of their sacred standing. I’ll make Jacob a curse and Israel an insult.”
Listen now, Jacob my servant, Israel, the one I’ve chosen.
Here’s what the LORD says, the one who made you, shaped you in the womb, and will help you: “Don’t be afraid, Jacob my servant. Don’t be afraid, Jeshurun, the one I’ve chosen.
I’ll pour water on the thirsty and streams on dry ground. I’ll pour my Spirit on your descendants and my blessing on your children.
They’ll spring up among the grass like willows beside flowing water.
One will say, ‘I belong to the LORD.’ Another will go by Jacob’s name. Another will write ‘Belonging to the LORD’ with their hand and honor the name of Israel.”
Here’s what the LORD of Armies, Israel’s King and Redeemer, says: “I’m the first and I’m the last. There’s no God besides me.
Who’s like me? Let them call it out, explain it, and lay it out in order for me, going back to when I established the people of long ago. Let them tell us what’s coming and what’s going to happen.
Don’t be scared or shaken. Didn’t I tell you long ago and make it known? You’re my witnesses. Is there another God besides me? There isn’t. I don’t know any other Rock.”
Everyone who carves an idol is chasing emptiness. The things they love won’t do them any good. Their own witnesses don’t see or understand, and they’ll end up ashamed.
Who shapes a god or casts an image that’s no use at all?
Look, all his partners will end up ashamed. The craftspeople are just human. Let them all gather and stand up. They’ll be scared and put to shame together.
The blacksmith takes an ax and works over hot coals. He shapes it with hammers and puts his muscle into it. Then he gets hungry and his strength gives out. Without water, he gets faint.
The carpenter stretches a line, marks the wood with a pencil, shapes it with planes, and marks it with a compass. He makes it look like a man, with all the beauty of a man, so it can live in a house.
He cuts down cedars and takes cypress and oak, letting a tree grow strong for himself among the forest trees. He plants a cypress, and the rain helps it grow.
The wood becomes fuel. He takes some and warms himself. He burns some and bakes bread. Then he makes a god, a carved figure, and gets down on the ground to worship it.
He burns part of it in the fire and uses some to roast meat. He eats till he’s full. Then he warms himself and says, “Ah, that feels good. I’m warm. I can see the fire.”
He makes the rest into a god, his carved idol. He bows to it, worships, and prays, “Save me! You’re my god!”
They have no idea. They don’t even think it through. He’s closed their eyes so they can’t see and closed their hearts so they can’t understand.

Nobody stops to think or has the sense to say, “I burned part of it in the fire. I baked bread over those coals, roasted meat, and ate it. Am I really going to turn the rest into something detestable? Am I about to bow to a log?”
He feeds on ashes. A heart that’s been fooled has led him off course. He can’t save himself or think to ask, “Isn’t this thing in my right hand a lie?”
Remember all this, Jacob and Israel. You’re my servant. I shaped you. You’re my servant, Israel, and I won’t forget you.
I’ve wiped away your rebellion like a thick cloud and your sins like a cloud swept away. Come back to me. I’ve redeemed you.
Sing, heavens! The LORD has done it! Shout, you depths of the earth! Break into song, mountains, forest, and every tree! The LORD has redeemed Jacob, and he’ll show his glory in Israel.
The LORD, your Redeemer, the one who shaped you in the womb, says, “I’m the LORD. I make everything. I stretched out the heavens by myself and spread out the earth on my own.
I ruin the signs of liars and drive fortune-tellers out of their minds. I turn the wise back and make their knowledge look silly.
I back up what my servant says and carry out what my messengers announce. I say of Jerusalem, ‘People will live there,’ and of Judah’s towns, ‘They’ll be rebuilt.’ I’ll raise up the ruined places.
I tell the deep, ‘Dry up,’ and say, ‘I’ll dry up your rivers.’
I say of Cyrus, ‘He’s my shepherd. He’ll do everything I want.’ I say of Jerusalem, ‘It’ll be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’”
Here’s what the LORD says to Cyrus, the one he anointed. “I’ve taken your right hand to bring nations under you and strip kings of their armor. I’ll open doors ahead of you. The gates won’t shut.
I’ll go ahead of you and smooth the rough ground. I’ll smash bronze doors and cut through iron bars.
I’ll give you treasures kept in darkness and riches tucked away in secret places. Then you’ll know I’m the LORD, the God of Israel, who called you by name.
For Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen, I’ve called you by name and given you a title, even though you haven’t known me.
I’m the LORD. There’s nobody else. There’s no God besides me. I’ll give you strength, even though you haven’t known me.
Then people from where the sun comes up to where it goes down will know there’s nobody besides me. I’m the LORD, and there’s nobody else.
I shape the light and create the dark. I bring peace and create calamity. I’m the LORD, the one who does all these things.
Rain down from above, you heavens. Let the skies pour out righteousness. Let the earth open up and produce salvation, and let righteousness sprout alongside it. I, the LORD, made it.

Trouble’s coming for the one fighting with their Maker, just one clay pot among all the clay pots on the ground! Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your own work say, ‘He has no hands’?
Trouble’s coming for anyone who says to a father, ‘What have you fathered?’ or to a mother, ‘What have you given birth to?’”
The LORD, the Holy One of Israel and its Maker, says, “You ask me what’s coming for my sons, and you try to tell me what to do with the work of my own hands!
I made the earth and created people on it. My own hands stretched out the heavens, and I gave orders to all their army.
I raised him up in righteousness, and I’ll straighten every road he takes. He’ll rebuild my city and set my exiles free without charging a price or taking a reward,” says the LORD of Armies.

The LORD says, “Egypt’s labor, Ethiopia’s goods, and those tall Sabeans will come over to you and be yours. They’ll follow you, coming over in chains. They’ll bow down to you and plead, ‘God really is with you, and there’s nobody else. There’s no other god.
You truly are a God who hides himself, God of Israel, the Savior.’”
Every one of them will end up ashamed and confused. The people who make idols will go off in confusion together.
The LORD will save Israel with a rescue that lasts forever. You’ll never be left ashamed or confused, for all ages to come.
The LORD made the heavens. He’s the God who shaped the earth, made it firm, and formed it for people to live on, never to be a wasteland. He says, “I’m the LORD. There’s nobody else.
I didn’t speak in secret from some dark corner of the earth. I didn’t tell Jacob’s children, ‘Look for me and get nowhere.’ I, the LORD, speak what’s righteous. I tell you what’s right.
“Gather and come. Come close together, you survivors from the nations. People who carry around a wooden idol and pray to a god that can’t save have no understanding.

State your case. Lay it out. Let them put their heads together. Who showed you this long ago? Who declared it way back? Wasn’t it me, the LORD? There’s no God besides me, a just God and a Savior. There’s nobody besides me.
“Turn to me and be saved, all you ends of the earth. I’m God, and there’s nobody else.
I’ve sworn by myself. A righteous word has left my mouth and won’t be taken back: every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will swear an oath.
People will say of me, ‘Only in the LORD are righteousness and strength.’” People will come to him, and everyone who raged against him will be put to shame.
All Israel’s descendants will be shown to be in the right through the LORD, and they’ll celebrate!
Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Animals and livestock are hauling their idols. The statues you used to carry are heavy loads on tired backs.
They stoop and bow down together. They couldn’t save the load, and now they’ve gone into captivity themselves.
“Listen to me, family of Jacob, and all of Israel’s family who are left. I’ve carried you since birth, held you up from the womb.
I’ll still be the same when you’re old. When your hair goes gray, I’ll carry you. I made you, and I’ll bear your weight. I’ll carry you and rescue you.
“Who could you compare me to? Who would you put on my level and say we’re the same?
Some people dump gold out of a bag and weigh silver on the scales. They hire a goldsmith, and he turns it into a god. Then down they go to worship it.
They hoist it onto their shoulders, carry it, and set it in place. It stands right there and can’t move. Somebody cries out to it, and it can’t answer. It can’t get them out of trouble.
“Remember this and stand firm. Get it back into your heads, you rebels.
Remember what happened long ago. I’m God, and there’s no other. I’m God, and nobody’s like me.
From the start I tell you how it’ll end. From long ago I tell you things that haven’t happened yet. I say, ‘My plan will stand. I’ll do everything I want to do.’
I call a hungry bird of prey from the east, the man who’ll carry out my plan from a distant land. I’ve spoken, and I’ll make it happen. I’ve planned it, and I’ll do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn hearts, you who are miles away from doing what’s right!
I’m bringing my righteousness close. It’s within reach, and my rescue won’t wait. I’ll bring salvation to Zion and give my glory to Israel.
“Get down and sit in the dust, virgin Daughter Babylon. Sit on the ground with no throne, Daughter of the Chaldeans. Nobody will call you soft and delicate anymore.
Grab the millstones and grind flour. Take off your veil, lift your skirt, bare your legs, and wade across the rivers.
You’ll be stripped naked, and your shame will be seen. I’ll take vengeance and spare nobody.”
Our Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel. His name is the LORD of Armies.
“Sit there in silence and go into the dark, Daughter of the Chaldeans. You’ll never be called the ruler of kingdoms again.
I was angry with my people. I treated my inheritance as unclean and handed them over to you. You didn’t show them any mercy. You put a crushing load even on the elderly.
You said, ‘I’ll be a princess forever.’ So you never took any of this to heart or thought about how it would end.
“Now hear this, you who live for pleasure and feel so secure. You tell yourself, ‘I’m the one, and there’s nobody else. I won’t end up a widow or know what it’s like to lose my children.’
Both will happen in an instant on the same day. You’ll lose your children and become a widow. You’ll feel the full weight of both, with all your sorcery and piles of spells.
You trusted your own wickedness. You said, ‘Nobody sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge twisted you around. You told yourself, ‘I’m the one, and there’s nobody else.’
So disaster will come on you, and you won’t know when it’s coming. Trouble will fall on you, and you won’t be able to fend it off. Sudden ruin will hit you before you can make sense of it.
“Go on, stand there with all those spells and all that sorcery you’ve worked at since you were young. See if you can gain anything. See if you can pull it off.
You’ve worn yourself out listening to so much advice. Now let the astrologers, the stargazers, and the ones who tell you what’s coming each month get up and save you from what’s about to happen.
Look, they’re like dry stubble. Fire will burn them up. They won’t be able to save themselves from the flames. This won’t be a coal to warm up by or a fire to sit around.
That’s how it’ll go with all that work you put in. The people who’ve done business with you since you were young will wander off in their own directions. Nobody will be there to save you.
“Hear this, family of Jacob, you who go by Israel’s name and came from the waters of Judah. You swear by the LORD’s name and call on Israel’s God, but there’s no truth or righteousness in it.
You call yourselves citizens of the holy city and lean on the God of Israel. The LORD of Armies is his name.
I told you long ago about the things that happened before. The words came out of my mouth. I revealed them, then made them happen all at once.
I knew how stubborn you were. Your neck was like an iron tendon and your forehead like bronze.
So I told you way back. I showed you before it happened so you couldn’t say, ‘My idol did it. My carved figure and my cast metal statue ordered it.’
You heard it. Now look at all of it. Aren’t you going to tell people? From now on I’m showing you new things, hidden things you didn’t know.
They’re being created now. They aren’t from long ago. Before today you never heard of them, so you can’t say, ‘I knew it already.’
You really didn’t hear or know. Your ears have been closed for a long time. I knew how deep your betrayal went, how you were called a rebel right from the womb.
For my name’s sake I’m putting off my anger. For the sake of my praise I’m holding it back so I don’t cut you off.
Look, I’ve refined you, though I didn’t refine you like silver. I chose you in the furnace of suffering.
For my own sake, yes, for my own sake, I’ll do it. How could I let my name be treated with contempt? I won’t give my glory to anyone else.
“Listen to me, Jacob, Israel, the one I called. I am he. I’m the first, and I’m the last.
My hand set the earth’s foundation. My right hand spread out the heavens. When I call to them, they all stand up together.
“Everybody gather around and listen! Who among them told you these things? The one the LORD loves will carry out his wishes against Babylon, and his arm will come against the Chaldeans.
I’m the one who spoke. I called him. I brought him here, and he’ll succeed in what he sets out to do.
“Come close and listen. From the start I haven’t spoken in secret. From the time it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord GOD has sent me with his Spirit.
Here’s what the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I’m the LORD your God. I teach you what’s good for you and lead you down the road you should take.
If only you’d paid attention to my commands! Your peace would’ve flowed like a river. Your righteousness would’ve rolled like the waves of the sea.
Your children would’ve been as many as the sand, your own descendants as many as its grains. Their name wouldn’t have been cut off or wiped out before me.”
Get out of Babylon! Run from the Chaldeans! Shout the news with joy. Tell it all the way to the far ends of the earth: “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!”
They didn’t get thirsty when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow out of the rock for them. He split the rock, and the water came gushing out.
“There’s no peace for the wicked,” says the LORD.
Listen to me, you islands. Pay attention, you peoples far away. The LORD called me before I was born. He said my name while I was still inside my mother.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me a polished arrow and kept me tucked in his quiver.
He told me, “You’re my servant, Israel. I’ll show my glory through you.”
But I said, “I’ve worked for nothing. I burned through my strength for nothing at all. Still, the justice I’m owed is with the LORD, and my reward is with my God.”
Now the LORD has spoken, the one who shaped me from the womb to serve him, to bring Jacob back and gather Israel to him. I matter in the LORD’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.

He says, “Bringing up Jacob’s tribes and bringing back the survivors of Israel is too small a job for my servant. I’ll make you a light for the nations too, so my salvation reaches the ends of the earth.”

Here’s what the LORD, Israel’s Redeemer and Holy One, says to the one people look down on, the one the nation can’t stand, the servant of rulers: “Kings will see you and get up from their seats. Princes will bow down in worship because the LORD is faithful. The Holy One of Israel has chosen you.”

The LORD says, “I answered you when the time was right. I helped you on the day of salvation. I’ll keep you safe and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and hand them back their abandoned inheritance.
You’ll say to the people in chains, ‘Come out!’ and to the ones in darkness, ‘Let yourselves be seen!’ They’ll feed along the roads, and even the bare hills will be pasture for them.
They won’t get hungry or thirsty. The heat and sun won’t beat them down, because the one who shows them mercy will lead them and guide them to springs of water.
I’ll turn all my mountains into roads, and my highways will be raised up.
Look, here they come from far away. Here are some from the north, some from the west, and some from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens! Celebrate, earth! Break into song, mountains! The LORD has comforted his people, and he’ll have compassion on the ones who are hurting.
But Zion said, “The LORD walked away from me. The Lord forgot about me.”
“Could a woman forget the baby she’s nursing? Could she stop caring about the child she carried? Even if she does forget, I won’t forget you!
Look, I’ve carved you into the palms of my hands. Your walls are always in front of me.
Your children are hurrying back. The people who ruined you and left you wrecked will leave you.
Look up. Look all around. They’re gathering and coming to you. As surely as I live,” says the LORD, “you’ll wear them like jewelry and dress yourself up with them like a bride.
“Your ruins, your empty places, and the land that was wrecked will be too small for all the people living there. The ones who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children you have after your loss will say right in your hearing, ‘It’s too crowded here. Make some room for me to live.’
Then you’ll say to yourself, ‘Who had these children for me? I lost my children and was left alone, an exile wandering from place to place. Who raised all these? I was on my own. Where were they?’”
The Lord GOD says, “Look, I’ll lift my hand to the nations and raise my banner for the peoples. They’ll bring your sons held close against their chests and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They’ll bow till their faces touch the ground and lick the dust at your feet. Then you’ll know I’m the LORD. The people who wait for me won’t be let down.”
Can you take plunder back from somebody powerful? Can you free the captives they’re entitled to hold?
But the LORD says, “Even the captives of the mighty will be taken back. Loot will be snatched from the fierce. I’ll fight the ones fighting you, and I’ll save your children.
I’ll feed your oppressors their own flesh. They’ll get drunk on their own blood like it’s sweet wine. Then everybody will know I’m the LORD, your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

The LORD says, “Where are your mother’s divorce papers, the ones I sent her away with? Or which of my creditors did I sell you to? Look, you were sold because of your wrongdoing, and your mother was sent away because of your rebellion.

When I came, why was nobody there? When I called, why did nobody answer? Has my hand gotten too short to redeem you? Have I run out of power to rescue you? At my word the sea dries up. I turn rivers into a desert. The fish stink because there’s no water, and they die of thirst.
I dress the heavens in darkness and cover them with sackcloth.”
The Lord GOD has given me the words of someone who’s been taught, so I know what to say to keep a worn-out person going. Morning after morning he wakes me, opens my ears, and teaches me to listen.
The Lord GOD opened my ears. I didn’t rebel or turn back.
I gave my back to the people beating me and my cheeks to the people pulling out my beard. I didn’t hide my face from insults or spit.
The Lord GOD will help me. That’s why I haven’t been put to shame. That’s why I’ve set my face as hard as flint. I know I won’t be let down.
The one who shows I’m in the right is close by. Who wants to bring charges against me? Let’s stand face to face. Who’s got a case against me? Come on over.
Look, the Lord GOD will help me! Who’s going to condemn me? They’ll all wear out like old clothes. Moths will eat them up.
Who here fears the LORD and listens to his servant? If you’re walking in the dark without a light, trust in the LORD’s name and lean on your God.
Look, all you who light a fire and surround yourselves with torches. Go on, walk in the flames you made and among the torches you lit. Here’s what you’ll get from my hand: you’ll lie down in sorrow.
“Listen to me, you who go after what’s right, you who seek the LORD. Look at the rock you were cut out of, the quarry you were dug from.
Look to Abraham your father and Sarah who gave birth to you. He was just one person when I called him. I blessed him and made him into many.

The LORD has comforted Zion. He’s brought comfort to every ruined place. He’s turned her wilderness into Eden, her desert into the LORD’s garden. You’ll find joy and gladness there, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
“Listen to me, my people. Hear me, my nation. Teaching will go out from me, and I’ll set my justice in place as a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is close. My rescue has already gone out. My arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me and put their trust in my arm.

Look up at the heavens, then look down at the earth. The heavens will disappear like smoke. The earth will wear out like old clothes, and its people will die off too. My salvation will last forever. My righteousness will never be undone.
“Listen to me, you who know what’s right, you people who carry my teaching in your hearts. Don’t fear what people say against you. Don’t let their insults shake you.
A moth will eat them like clothes, and a worm will eat them like wool. My righteousness will last forever, and my salvation will reach every generation.”
Wake up! Wake up and put on strength, arm of the LORD! Wake up like you did way back in the days of our ancestors! Weren’t you the one who cut Rahab to pieces and pierced the monster?
Weren’t you the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made a road across the seabed for the people you redeemed?
The people the LORD ransomed will come back. They’ll sing their way into Zion, crowned with joy that lasts forever. Gladness and joy will be theirs, and grief and sighing will run away.
“I’m the one who comforts you. So why are you scared of people who’ll die, of a human being who’ll end up like grass?

Did you forget the LORD who made you, the one who stretched out the heavens and set the earth on its foundations? Are you going to live in fear all day long because your oppressor is furious and getting ready to destroy you? Where’s all that rage now?
The exile in chains will be set free soon. He won’t die and go down into the pit. He won’t run out of bread.
I’m the LORD your God. I stir up the sea till its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is my name.
I put my words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of my hand. I did it to plant the heavens, lay the earth’s foundations, and tell Zion, ‘You’re my people.’”
Wake up! Wake up and stand, Jerusalem! The LORD handed you the cup of his anger, and you drank it. You drained the bowl that makes you stagger, right down to the bottom.
Of all the sons she gave birth to, there’s nobody to guide her. Of all the sons she raised, nobody takes her by the hand.
Two disasters hit you, and who’s there to grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, famine and the sword. How can I comfort you?
Your sons have collapsed. They’re lying at every street corner like an antelope caught in a net. They’ve felt the full force of the LORD’s anger and your God’s rebuke.
So hear this now, you who’ve been crushed and are reeling like you’re drunk, though you haven’t touched wine:
Your Lord GOD, the God who argues his people’s case, says, “Look, I’ve taken the cup that makes you stagger right out of your hand, the bowl of my anger. You’ll never drink it again.
I’ll hand it to the people who tormented you, the ones who told you, ‘Get down so we can walk over you.’ You flattened your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk over.”
Wake up! Wake up and put on your strength, Zion! Put on your finest clothes, Jerusalem, holy city. The uncircumcised and the unclean won’t enter you anymore.
Shake off the dust! Get up and sit upright, Jerusalem! Take the chains off your neck, captive Daughter Zion!
The LORD says, “You were sold for nothing, and you’ll be redeemed without paying a thing.”
The Lord GOD says, “My people first went down to Egypt to live there. Then the Assyrian oppressed them for no reason.
“So now what am I doing here,” says the LORD, “when my people have been taken away for nothing? Their rulers mock them,” says the LORD, “and my name is insulted all day long, over and over.
So my people will know my name. On that day they’ll know that I’m the one speaking. Look, it’s me.”
How beautiful are the feet of the one coming over the mountains with good news, announcing peace, bringing good news, proclaiming salvation, and telling Zion, “Your God reigns!”
Your lookouts lift their voices. They sing together because they’ll see it with their own eyes when the LORD comes back to Zion.
Burst out with joy! Sing together, you ruins of Jerusalem. The LORD has comforted his people. He’s redeemed Jerusalem.
The LORD has bared his holy arm where every nation can see it. All the ends of the earth have seen our God save his people.
Get out! Go, get out of there! Don’t touch anything unclean. Leave that place. Make yourselves clean, you who carry the LORD’s vessels.
You won’t have to hurry out or run for your lives. The LORD will go ahead of you, and the God of Israel will guard you from behind.
Look, my servant will act wisely. He’ll be raised up, lifted up, and set very high.
So many people were shocked at the sight of you. His appearance was disfigured more than anyone’s, his body more than any human being’s.
In the same way, he’ll cleanse many nations. Kings will shut their mouths when they see him. They’ll see what nobody had told them about and understand what they’d never heard.
Who believed what we told them? Who got to see the LORD’s arm at work?
He grew up in front of him like a tender shoot, like a root pushing out of dry ground. He had no looks or majesty to catch our eye. When we looked at him, there was no beauty that made us want him.
People looked down on him and rejected him. He knew suffering and sickness firsthand. People turned their faces away from him in disgust, and we didn’t give him any respect.
He really did carry our sickness and take our suffering on himself. We thought he was plagued, struck by God, and made to suffer.
He was pierced because of our rebellion. He was crushed because of our wrongs. The punishment that brought us peace landed on him, and his wounds are how we’re healed.
We all wandered off like sheep. Every one of us went our own way, and the LORD put all our wrongdoing on him.
They oppressed him and made him suffer, but he didn’t open his mouth. Like a lamb led away to be killed, like a sheep that stays silent in front of the ones shearing it, he didn’t open his mouth.
Oppression and judgment swept him away. Who in his generation stopped to think that he was cut off from the land of the living and struck down for my people’s disobedience?
They gave him a grave with the wicked and put him with a rich man in his death, even though he’d done no violence and never spoken a lie.
Yet the LORD chose to bruise him and make him suffer. When you make his life an offering for sin, he’ll see his descendants. He’ll live long, and what the LORD wants will succeed through him.
After the anguish he’s gone through, he’ll see the light and be satisfied. By the knowledge of himself, my righteous servant will put many people in the right, and he’ll carry their wrongdoing.

So I’ll give him a share with the great, and he’ll split the spoils with the strong. He poured out his life to death and was counted with the rebels. He carried the sins of many and pleaded for the people who rebelled.

“Sing, you who couldn’t have children and never gave birth! Burst into song and shout, you who never went through labor! The woman left alone has more children than the wife with a husband,” says the LORD.
“Make more room for your tent. Stretch your tent curtains out wide. Don’t hold back. Lengthen the ropes and make the stakes stronger.
You’ll spread out to the right and left. Your descendants will take possession of nations and settle in cities that were left empty.
“Don’t be afraid. You won’t be put to shame. Don’t let confusion shake you. You won’t be disgraced. You’ll forget the shame of being young and won’t remember the humiliation of being a widow.
The one who made you is your husband. His name is the LORD of Armies. The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer. He’ll be called the God of the whole earth.
The LORD has called you like a wife who was left behind and is hurting deep inside, like a wife married young and then cast aside,” says your God.
“I left you for a short moment, but I’ll gather you back with deep compassion.
In a flood of anger, I turned my face away from you for a moment. But I’ll have mercy on you with faithful love that lasts forever,” says the LORD who redeems you.
“This is like the waters of Noah to me. I swore that Noah’s waters would never cover the earth again. Just like that, I’ve sworn I won’t be angry with you or rebuke you.
Mountains can move away and hills can be shaken out of place. My faithful love won’t leave you, and my promise of peace won’t be taken away,” says the LORD who has mercy on you.
“You’ve been beaten up, tossed by storms, and left with nobody to comfort you. Look, I’ll set your stones in beautiful colors and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I’ll make your towers of rubies, your gates of sparkling gems, and every wall out of precious stones.
The LORD will teach all your children, and your children will have deep peace.
You’ll be firmly established in righteousness. Oppression will be far from you, and you won’t be afraid. Terror won’t come anywhere near you.
Look, people may gather against you, but I won’t be the one sending them. Whoever comes against you will fall because of you.
“Look, I created the blacksmith who blows the coals into flame and forges a weapon for the job. I also created the destroyer to destroy.
No weapon made to come against you will win. You’ll prove every voice that accuses you in court wrong. That’s what my servants inherit. Their righteousness comes from me,” says the LORD.
“Hey, every thirsty one of you, come to the water! No money? Come anyway. Buy and eat! Come get wine and milk with no money and no price to pay.
Why spend your money on stuff that isn’t bread or work for stuff that leaves you empty? Listen closely to me. Eat what’s good and let your soul enjoy the rich food.
Turn your ear this way and come to me. Listen, and you’ll live. I’ll make a covenant with you that lasts forever, the same sure mercies I promised David.
Look, I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples.
Look, you’ll call a nation you don’t know, and a nation that didn’t know you will come running because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel. He’s given you glory.”
Look for the LORD while you can find him. Call out to him while he’s close.

Let the wicked walk away from their ways and people who do wrong let go of their thoughts. Let them come back to the LORD. He’ll have mercy on them. Let them come back to our God. He’ll forgive freely.
“My thoughts aren’t your thoughts, and your ways aren’t my ways,” says the LORD.
“The heavens rise high above the earth. That’s how far my ways rise above yours and how far my thoughts rise above yours.
Rain and snow come down from the sky and don’t go back there without watering the earth. They make it sprout and grow, giving seed to the person sowing and bread to the person eating.
That’s how it is with a word that leaves my mouth. It won’t come back empty. It’ll do what I want it to do, and it’ll succeed at what I sent it for.
You’ll go out with joy and be led out in peace. Mountains and hills will burst into song ahead of you, and every tree in the fields will clap its hands.
Where thorns grew, cypress trees will come up. Where briars grew, myrtle trees will come up. It’ll bring honor to the LORD’s name and stand as a lasting sign that never gets cut down.”
The LORD says, “Stand up for justice and do what’s right. My rescue is close, and my righteousness is about to be seen.
Blessed is the person who does this and holds on tight to it, who keeps the Sabbath holy and keeps their hands from doing anything evil.”
A foreigner who’s joined the LORD shouldn’t say, “The LORD’s definitely going to separate me from his people.” A eunuch shouldn’t say, “Look at me. I’m just a dried-up tree.”
The LORD says, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what makes me glad, and hold tightly to my covenant,
I’ll give a memorial and a name in my house, inside my walls, better than sons or daughters could give. I’ll give them a name that lasts forever and never gets cut off.
The foreigners who join themselves to the LORD, who serve him, love the LORD’s name, and become his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath holy and holds tightly to my covenant,

I’ll bring them to my holy mountain. I’ll give them joy in my house of prayer. I’ll accept their burnt offerings and their sacrifices on my altar, because my house will be called a house of prayer for every people.”
The Lord GOD, who gathers those driven out of Israel, says, “I’ll gather others to him too, along with his own who are already gathered.”
All you animals out in the fields, come and eat your fill, and all you animals in the forest, come too.
His lookouts are blind. None of them know what’s going on. They’re all dogs that can’t bark, lying around dreaming because they love to sleep.
These dogs are greedy. Nothing’s ever enough. They’re shepherds who don’t understand. Every last one has turned their own way, chasing whatever they can get.
“Come on,” they say. “I’ll get wine. Let’s fill up on strong drink. Tomorrow will be just like today, only bigger and better.”
Good people die and nobody takes it to heart. Merciful people are taken away, and nobody stops to think that the righteous are being taken out of the reach of evil.
They enter into peace. They rest in their beds, every one of them who lived right.
“But you, come here, children of a sorceress, descendants of adulterers and prostitutes.
Who are you making fun of? Who are you opening your mouths wide and sticking your tongues out at? Aren’t you children of rebellion, born of lies?
You work yourselves into a frenzy among the oaks, under every green tree. You kill children down in the valleys, in the cracks beneath the rocks.
The smooth stones in the valley are your share. That’s your lot. You’ve poured out a drink offering to them and made them an offering. Am I supposed to be satisfied with that?
You put your bed on a high mountain. You went up there to offer a sacrifice too.

You set up your memorial behind the doors and doorposts. You exposed yourself to someone besides me and climbed up. You made your bed bigger and struck a deal with them. You loved what you saw on their bed.
You came to the king with oil and piled on the perfume. You sent envoys far away and lowered yourself all the way to Sheol.
Your long trips wore you out, but you never said, ‘This is pointless.’ You found your strength again, so you didn’t give out.
“Who scared you enough to make you lie? Why didn’t you remember me or take me to heart? Haven’t I kept quiet for a long time? Is that why you don’t fear me?
I’ll tell everyone about your righteousness, and your works won’t do you any good.

When you cry for help, let that whole collection of yours rescue you. The wind will take them. One breath will sweep them all away. Whoever comes to me for shelter will possess the land and inherit my holy mountain.”
He’ll say, “Build it up! Build it up! Get the road ready! Clear anything that could trip my people off their path.”

The high and lofty one who lives in eternity, whose name is Holy, says, “I live high up in a holy place, and I live with those who are humble and sorry for their wrongs. I bring the spirit of the humble back to life and revive the heart of those who are sorry.
I won’t keep arguing forever or stay angry always. The spirit would give out before me, the very lives I made.
I was angry over his greedy wrongdoing, so I struck him. I turned away in anger, and he kept going the wrong way his heart wanted.
I’ve seen how he lives, and I’ll heal him. I’ll lead him and bring comfort back to him and the people mourning with him.
I put these words on people’s lips: Peace, peace to those far away and to those close by,” says the LORD. “I’ll heal them.”
But wicked people are like a rough sea that can’t settle down. Its waters keep throwing up muck and mud.
“There’s no peace for the wicked,” says my God.
“Shout it out! Don’t hold back! Raise your voice like a trumpet! Tell my people how they’ve rebelled, and tell Jacob’s family about their sins.

They come looking for me every day, acting like they love learning my ways. They ask me for fair rulings as if they were a nation that did right and stuck to their God’s rules. They love acting close to God.

‘Why did we fast and you didn’t see it?’ they ask. ‘Why did we put ourselves through all that and you didn’t notice?’ Look, on the day you’re fasting, you chase whatever pleases you and push all your workers around.
You fast and end up fighting and arguing, throwing punches you have no right to throw. You can’t fast like that today and expect your voice to reach heaven.

Is that the fast I chose? Just a day to make yourself look humble? Is it about hanging your head like a reed and spreading sackcloth and ashes under yourself? You call that fasting? You think that’s a day the LORD accepts?
“Here’s the fast I chose. Loosen the ties of wickedness. Undo the straps of the yoke. Let the oppressed go free. Break every yoke.
Share your bread with hungry people. Bring poor people without a home into yours. When you see someone without clothes, cover them. Don’t turn away from your own flesh and blood.
Then your light will break through like the morning, and you’ll heal fast. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and the LORD’s glory will guard you from behind.
Then you’ll call, and the LORD will answer. You’ll cry for help, and he’ll say, ‘I’m right here.’ “Get rid of the yoke among you, the finger-pointing, and the hateful talk.
Give yourself to hungry people and meet the needs of those who are suffering. Then your light will rise in the dark, and your deepest gloom will be as bright as noon.
The LORD will keep guiding you. He’ll satisfy you in dry places and make your bones strong. You’ll be like a garden with plenty of water, like a spring that never runs dry.
Your people will rebuild the old ruins. You’ll raise up foundations laid generations ago. People will call you Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Roads Where People Live.

“Hold yourself back on the Sabbath from doing whatever pleases you on my holy day. Call the Sabbath a delight and honor the LORD’s holy day. Honor it by leaving your own ways, giving your own pleasures a rest, and setting aside your own talk.
Then you’ll find your joy in the LORD. I’ll make you ride on the heights of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob.” The LORD himself has spoken.
Look, the LORD’s hand hasn’t gotten too short to save you. His ears haven’t gone dull so he can’t hear you.
Your wrongdoing has put distance between you and your God. Your sins have made him turn his face away so he won’t hear.
Your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with wrongdoing. Your lips tell lies, and your tongue mutters evil.
Nobody brings a case honestly or argues it with the truth. They trust empty claims and tell lies. They conceive trouble and give birth to wrongdoing.
They hatch viper eggs and spin spiderwebs. Anyone who eats their eggs dies, and crush one open and a viper comes out.
Those webs won’t make clothes, and they can’t cover themselves with the things they make. What they do is crooked, and their hands are full of violence.
Their feet rush toward evil. They can’t wait to spill innocent blood. Their thoughts are full of wrongdoing. They leave ruin and destruction wherever they go.
They don’t know the road to peace. There’s no justice on their routes. They’ve made themselves crooked roads, and nobody walking them knows peace.
That’s why justice is so far from us and righteousness can’t reach us. We’re looking for light and finding darkness. We want brightness, but we walk in the gloom.
We feel along the wall like people who are blind. We reach around like we have no eyes. We trip at noon as if it were dusk. Among the strong, we’re like dead people.
We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We look for justice and find none. We look for rescue, but it’s far away from us.
Our rebellions have piled up before you. Our sins speak against us. We carry those rebellions around with us, and we know exactly what we’ve done:
we rebelled against the LORD and denied him. We turned away from following our God. We talked about oppression and revolt, making up lies in our hearts and then saying them out loud.
Justice has been pushed back, and righteousness stands far off. Truth has tripped and fallen in the street, and honesty can’t even get in.
Truth is missing, and anybody who turns away from evil becomes a target. The LORD saw it, and he was displeased that there was no justice.
He saw there was nobody there. He was appalled that nobody stepped in. So his own arm brought him victory, and his righteousness held him up.
He put on righteousness like armor over his chest and salvation like a helmet on his head. He dressed himself in vengeance and wrapped himself in passion like a cloak.
He’ll pay people back in line with what they did: fury for his opponents and what his enemies deserve. He’ll give the islands what they’re due too.
So people in the west will fear the LORD’s name, and people where the sun rises will fear his glory. He’ll come like a rushing river driven by the LORD’s breath.
“A Redeemer will come to Zion and to the people of Jacob who turn away from rebellion,” says the LORD.

“Here’s my covenant with them,” says the LORD. “My Spirit is on you, and I’ve put my words in your mouth. They won’t leave your mouth, or your children’s mouths, or your grandchildren’s mouths,” says the LORD, “from now on and forever.”
“Get up and shine! Your light is here, and the LORD’s glory has risen over you!
Look, darkness will cover the earth and thick darkness will cover its peoples. But the LORD will rise over you, and his glory will be seen on you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
“Look up and look around. They’re all gathering and coming to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be carried in people’s arms.
Then you’ll see it and light up. Your heart will race and swell with joy, because the riches of the sea will flow your way and the wealth of nations will come to you.
Camels will cover the land, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. Everyone from Sheba will show up, bringing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the LORD’s praises.
All Kedar’s flocks will be gathered to you. Nebaioth’s rams will serve you. They’ll be accepted as offerings on my altar, and I’ll make my glorious house beautiful.
“Who are these flying in like a cloud, like doves coming back to their windows?

The islands will wait for me, with the ships of Tarshish leading the way. They’ll bring your sons from far away with their silver and gold, for the name of the LORD your God, for the Holy One of Israel, because he’s given you glory.
“Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. I struck you when I was angry, but in my kindness I’ve had mercy on you.
Your gates will stay open all the time. They won’t shut by day or at night, so people can bring you the wealth of the nations with their kings led captive.
Any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will perish. Those nations will be completely wiped out.
“Lebanon’s glory will come to you: cypress, pine, and box trees together to make my sanctuary beautiful. I’ll give glory to the place where my feet rest.
The children of the people who hurt you will come bowing. Everyone who looked down on you will bow right at your feet. They’ll call you the LORD’s City, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
“You were abandoned and hated, with nobody even passing through. I’ll make you a place of lasting splendor, a joy for generations.
You’ll drink the milk of the nations and nurse at royal breasts. Then you’ll know that I’m the LORD, your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
I’ll bring gold instead of bronze, silver instead of iron, bronze instead of wood, and iron instead of stones. I’ll make peace your governor and righteousness your ruler.
Nobody will hear of violence in your land anymore, or ruin and destruction within your borders. You’ll call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
You won’t need the sun for light during the day or the glow of the moon for light at night. The LORD will be your light forever, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun won’t go down again, and your moon won’t disappear. The LORD will be your light forever, and your days of mourning will end.
All your people will be righteous. They’ll inherit the land forever. They’re a branch I planted, the work of my hands, so I’ll be glorified.
The smallest family will become a thousand, and the little one will become a strong nation. I’m the LORD. When the time comes, I’ll make it happen fast.”

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD anointed me to bring good news to the humble. He sent me to bandage broken hearts, announce freedom to captives, and release to the people in chains,
