to announce the year of the LORD’s favor and our God’s day of vengeance, to comfort everyone who’s grieving,

and to care for those who grieve in Zion. He sent me to give them a garland in place of ashes, oil of joy in place of mourning, and praise to wear in place of a heavy spirit. People will call them trees of righteousness, planted by the LORD so he’ll be glorified.
They’ll rebuild the ancient ruins. They’ll raise up places that used to be wrecked and fix cities that have been in ruins for generations.
Strangers will tend your flocks. Foreigners will work your fields and vineyards.
You’ll be called the LORD’s priests. People will call you the servants of our God. You’ll live on the wealth of the nations and take pride in their glory.
You’ll receive a double share in place of shame. In place of disgrace, they’ll celebrate their share. They’ll own twice as much in their own land, and their joy will last forever.
“I’m the LORD, and I love justice. I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I’ll faithfully give them what’s due and make a covenant with them that lasts forever.
Their children will be known among the nations, their descendants among the peoples. Everybody who sees them will know they’re the people the LORD blessed.”

I’ll celebrate with everything I’ve got in the LORD. My whole soul will be glad in my God. He dressed me in salvation and covered me with a robe of righteousness, like a groom putting on a garland and a bride putting on her jewels.
The earth makes new shoots grow, and a garden makes what you plant spring up. That’s how the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up in front of every nation.
For Zion’s sake I won’t stay quiet. For Jerusalem’s sake I won’t rest until her righteousness shines like dawn and her salvation burns like a lamp.
Nations will see your righteousness, and every king will see your glory. You’ll have a new name, straight from the LORD’s mouth.
You’ll be a beautiful crown in the LORD’s hand, a royal headpiece in the hand of your God.
Nobody will call you Forsaken anymore or call your land Desolate. You’ll be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah. The LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
Just as a young man marries a young woman who’s a virgin, your sons will marry you. Just as a groom celebrates over his bride, your God will celebrate over you.
Jerusalem, I’ve posted lookouts on your walls. They’ll never go quiet, day or night. You who call on the LORD, don’t take a break,
and don’t give him a break until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it the praise of the earth.
The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by his strong arm: “I won’t give your grain to your enemies to eat anymore. Foreigners won’t drink the new wine you worked so hard for.
The people who harvested the grain will eat it and praise the LORD. The ones who gathered the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of my sanctuary.”
Go through! Go through the gates! Get the road ready for the people! Build it up! Build up that highway! Clear away the stones! Raise a banner for the peoples.
Look, the LORD has announced it to the farthest ends of the earth: “Tell Daughter Zion, ‘Look, your salvation is coming! His reward comes with him, and what he’ll give in return goes ahead of him!’”
They’ll be called “The Holy People, the LORD’s Redeemed.” You’ll be called “Sought Out, a City That Wasn’t Forsaken.”
Who’s this coming from Edom with dyed clothes from Bozrah? Who’s this dressed in splendor and marching in such strength? “It’s me. I speak in righteousness, and I’m mighty enough to save.”
Why are your clothes red? Why do you look like someone who’s been stomping grapes in a wine vat?

“I worked the winepress alone. Nobody from the peoples was there with me. I stomped them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood splashed onto my clothes and stained everything I was wearing.
I had the day of vengeance in my heart, and the year for redeeming my people had come.
I looked around. Nobody was there to help. I was amazed that nobody backed me up. So my own arm won the victory for me, and my own wrath kept me going.
I trampled the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my rage. I poured their lifeblood out onto the earth.”

I’ll talk about all the ways the LORD has shown us faithful love. I’ll praise the LORD for everything he’s given us and all the great good he’s done for Israel’s family, out of his mercy and the abundance of his faithful love.
He said, “Surely they’re my people, children who won’t deal falsely.” So he became their Savior.
Every time they suffered, he suffered too, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and compassion, he redeemed them. He lifted them up and carried them through all those days long ago.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned against them and became their enemy. He fought them himself.
Then he remembered those days long ago, Moses and his people. “Where’s the one who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where’s the one who put his Holy Spirit among them?”
Who put his glorious arm at Moses’ right hand? Who split the waters ahead of them to make a name for himself that would last forever?
Who led them through the deep like a horse crossing open country, so they didn’t stumble?
Like cattle going down into a valley, the LORD’s Spirit gave them rest. That’s how you led your people to make a glorious name for yourself.
Look down from heaven and see us from your holy and glorious home. Where’s your passion? Where are your mighty acts? You’re holding back your deep feelings and compassion from me.
You’re our Father, even though Abraham doesn’t know us and Israel doesn’t recognize us. You, LORD, are our Father. Our Redeemer from Everlasting is your name.
LORD, why do you make us wander off your paths and harden our hearts so we don’t fear you? Come back for your servants, the tribes that are your inheritance.
Your holy people held it for only a little while. Now our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.
We’ve become like people you never ruled, like people who were never called by your name.
If only you’d tear open the heavens and come down! The mountains would shake in front of you,
like fire lighting up dry brush or making water boil. Make your name known to your enemies so the nations shake when you show up!
You did awesome things we never saw coming. You came down, and the mountains shook in front of you.
From way back, nobody’s ever heard of or seen another God like you, a God who acts for those who wait for him.
You meet people who take joy in doing what’s right, who remember you by following your ways. Look, you were angry, and we sinned. We’ve been at it a long time. Can we still be saved?
We’ve all become unclean, and all the right things we’ve done are like filthy clothes. We all wither like leaves, and our own wrongs blow us away like the wind.
Nobody calls on your name or gets up to grab hold of you. You’ve hidden your face from us and let our wrongdoing consume us.
But now, LORD, you’re our Father. We’re the clay, and you’re the potter. Every one of us is a piece of work from your hand.
Don’t be furious, LORD. Don’t hold our wrongs in your memory forever. Please, take a look. We’re all your people.
Your holy cities have turned into wilderness. Zion is a wilderness. Jerusalem is a ruin.
Our holy and beautiful house, where our ancestors praised you, went up in flames. Everything we loved has been laid waste.
After all this, LORD, will you still hold back? Will you stay silent and punish us so severely?
“People who never asked about me came looking for answers. People who didn’t seek me found me. I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’ to a nation that didn’t go by my name.
All day I held out my hands to rebellious people who take a bad road because they follow their own ideas.
They provoke me to my face constantly, making sacrifices in gardens and burning incense on bricks.
They sit among graves and spend the night in hidden places. They eat pork and keep broth made from disgusting things in their pots.
They say, ‘Keep to yourself. Don’t get near me. I’m holier than you.’ They’re like smoke up my nose, like a fire that burns all day.
“Look, it’s written right here in front of me. I won’t stay silent. I’ll pay them back. I’ll put it right into their laps.

I’ll repay your wrongs and your ancestors’ wrongs together,” says the LORD. “They burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. First I’ll measure out what their deeds earned and put it right into their laps.”
The LORD says, “When there’s new wine in a bunch of grapes, somebody says, ‘Don’t trash it. There’s a blessing in there.’ I’ll do the same for the sake of my servants. I won’t destroy them all.
I’ll bring descendants out of Jacob and someone from Judah to inherit my mountains. The people I chose will inherit the land. My servants will live there.
Sharon will be a pen for flocks, and the Valley of Achor will be a place for herds to lie down. It’ll be for my people who sought me.
“But you turned your back on the LORD. You forgot my holy mountain. You set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny.

I’ll destine you for the sword. You’ll all bow down to be slaughtered. I called, and you didn’t answer. I spoke, and you wouldn’t listen. You did what was evil in my eyes and chose what gave me no joy.”
So the Lord GOD says, “Look, my servants will eat, and you’ll be hungry. My servants will drink, and you’ll be thirsty. My servants will celebrate, and you’ll be put to shame.
My servants will sing because their hearts are full of joy. You’ll cry because your hearts are hurting and wail because your spirits are crushed.
The people I chose will use your name as a curse. The Lord GOD will put you to death, and he’ll give his servants another name.

Then anyone who asks for a blessing on earth will call on the God of truth, and anyone who takes an oath on earth will swear by the God of truth. The old troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
“Look, I’m creating new heavens and a new earth. Nobody will remember what was before, and it won’t cross their minds.
Be glad and celebrate forever over what I’m creating. Look, I’m creating Jerusalem to be a delight and its people to be a joy.
I’ll rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in my people. No one there will hear the sound of weeping or crying again.

“Never again will a baby live only a few days or an old person die before finishing their years. Someone who dies at a hundred will be considered young, and a sinner who reaches a hundred will be under a curse.
They’ll build homes and live in them. They’ll plant vineyards and eat the fruit.

They won’t build for somebody else to move in or plant for somebody else to eat. My people will live as long as trees, and the people I chose will have plenty of time to enjoy what they made with their own hands.
Their work won’t be wasted, and they won’t have children only to see disaster strike them. They’re the children of people the LORD has blessed, and their descendants are with them.
Before they call, I’ll answer. While they’re still talking, I’ll hear.
The wolf and the lamb will eat together. The lion will eat straw like an ox, and dust will be the serpent’s food. Nothing will harm or destroy anywhere on my holy mountain,” says the LORD.
The LORD says, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? Where could I rest?
My hand made all of this. That’s how everything came to be,” says the LORD. “Here’s the one I’ll look to: the poor person whose spirit is humbled and who trembles at my word.

Someone who kills an ox is like someone who kills a person. Someone who sacrifices a lamb is like someone who breaks a dog’s neck. Someone who brings an offering is like someone offering pig’s blood. Someone who burns frankincense is like someone who blesses an idol. They’ve chosen to do things their way, and they love the disgusting things they do.

So I’ll choose their delusions and bring the very things they fear on them. I called and nobody answered. I spoke and they didn’t listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what gave me no joy.”

Hear the LORD’s word, you who tremble at what he says. “Your own brothers hate you and threw you out because of my name. They said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified so we can see your joy.’ They’re the ones who’ll end up ashamed.
Hear the uproar from the city! Hear the voice from the temple! It’s the LORD’s voice giving his enemies what they deserve.
“Before she went into labor, she gave birth. Before the pains came, she delivered a son.

Who’s ever heard of such a thing? Who’s ever seen anything like it? Can a land be born in a day? Can a whole nation come into being all at once? The moment Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
Would I bring a child to the moment of birth and then hold back the delivery?” says the LORD. “Would I, the one who makes birth happen, close the womb?” says your God.
“Celebrate with Jerusalem. Be glad for her, all of you who love her. Celebrate right along with her, all you who’ve mourned over her.
Then you can nurse until you’re satisfied at her comforting breasts. You can drink deeply and delight in how full of glory she is.”
The LORD says, “Look, I’ll send peace flowing to her like a river and the glory of nations like a stream overflowing its banks. You’ll nurse. You’ll be carried at her side and bounced on her knees.
I’ll comfort you like a mother comforts her child. You’ll find comfort in Jerusalem.”
You’ll see it, and your hearts will be glad. Your bones will grow strong like tender grass. The LORD will show his hand to his servants and his anger to his enemies.
Look, the LORD will come with fire. His chariots will roar in like a whirlwind. He’ll let loose his fierce anger and deliver his rebuke in flames.
The LORD will judge all humanity with fire and with his sword. Many will be killed by the LORD.

“People set themselves apart and make themselves clean to go into the gardens. They follow the one in the middle and eat pork, disgusting things, and mice. They’ll all come to an end together,” says the LORD.
“I know what they do and what they think. The time is coming when I’ll bring together all nations and languages. They’ll come and see my glory.

“I’ll set a sign among them and send the survivors to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan and distant islands that haven’t heard of me or seen my glory. They’ll tell the nations about my glory.

They’ll bring all your brothers and sisters out of every nation as an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots and covered stretchers, on mules and camels, to my holy mountain, Jerusalem,” says the LORD. “It’ll be like the people of Israel bringing their offering into the LORD’s house in a clean container.
I’ll choose some of them as priests and Levites too,” says the LORD.
“The new heavens and the new earth I’ll make will stay before me,” says the LORD. “That’s how your descendants and your name will last.
From one new moon to the next, and from one Sabbath to the next, all humanity will come to worship before me,” says the LORD.
“They’ll go out and see the dead bodies of the people who rebelled against me. The worms feeding on them won’t die, their fire won’t go out, and all humanity will find them repulsive.”
